verses.1:1: The vision which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw, which he saw against Judea and against Jerusalem, in the reign of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, who reigned over Judea.
verses.1:2: Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth, for the Lord has spoken: "I have brought forth sons and exalted them, yet they have rejected Me.
verses.1:3: An ox knows its owner, and a donkey its master's manger; yet Israel does not know Me, and the people do not understand Me."
verses.1:4: Woe, sinful nation, a people full of sins, a wicked seed, lawless sons! You have forsaken the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger.
verses.1:5: Why should you still be struck, adding lawlessness? Every head is given to pain, and every heart to grief.
verses.1:6: From the feet to the head, neither wound nor bruise nor festering blow—there is no poultice to apply, nor oil, nor bandages.
verses.1:7: Your land is desolate, your cities are burned with fire; strangers devour your country before your eyes, and it has been laid waste, overthrown by foreign peoples.
verses.1:8: The daughter of Zion shall be forsaken like a booth in a vineyard, and like a watchman's hut in a cucumber field, like a besieged city.
verses.1:9: And if the Lord of hosts had not left us a seed, we would have become like Sodom, and we would have been made like Gomorrah.
verses.1:10: Hear the word of the Lord, you rulers of Sodom; give heed to the law of God, you people of Gomorrah.
verses.1:11: "What is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?" says the Lord. "I am full of burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of lambs and the blood of bulls and goats I do not desire,
verses.1:12: not even if you come to appear before Me. For who has required these things from your hands? To tread My court
verses.1:13: you shall not continue; if you bring fine flour, it is vain; incense is an abomination to Me. Your new moons and the Sabbaths and a great day I cannot endure; fasting and idleness
verses.1:14: and your new moons and your feasts My soul hates; you have become a surfeit to Me; I will no longer forgive your sins.
verses.1:15: Whenever you stretch forth your hands, I will turn My eyes away from you; and even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
verses.1:16: Wash yourselves, become clean, remove the wicked deeds from your souls before My eyes; cease from your wicked deeds,
verses.1:17: learn to do good, seek out justice, rescue the wronged, judge for the orphan, and vindicate the widow.
verses.1:18: And come, let us settle the dispute," says the Lord. "Even if your sins are like crimson, I will make them white as snow; and if they are like scarlet, I will make them white as wool.
verses.1:19: And if you are willing and listen to Me, you shall eat the good things of the land;
verses.1:20: but if you are not willing and do not listen to Me, a sword shall devour you," for the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things.
verses.1:21: How has the faithful city Zion, full of justice, become a harlot? In her righteousness once lodged, yet now murderers!
verses.1:22: Your silver is debased; your tavern keepers mix the wine with water.
verses.1:23: Your rulers are disobedient, companions of thieves, loving bribes, pursuing recompense, not judging for orphans, and not heeding the cause of widows.
verses.1:24: Therefore thus says the Lord, the Sovereign of hosts: "Woe to the mighty men of Israel! For My wrath shall not cease against the adversaries, and I will execute judgment upon My enemies.
verses.1:25: And I will bring My hand upon you and refine you in fire to purity, and I will destroy the disobedient, and I will remove all lawless ones from you;
verses.1:26: and I will appoint your judges as before, and your counselors as from the beginning; and after these things you shall be called 'City of Righteousness, Faithful Mother City Zion.'"
verses.1:27: For with judgment her captivity shall be saved, and with mercy.
verses.1:28: And the lawless and the sinners shall be crushed together, and those who forsake the Lord shall be utterly consumed.
verses.1:29: For they shall be put to shame because of their idols which they themselves desired, and they have been put to shame over the gardens which they coveted.
verses.1:30: For they shall be like a terebinth that has shed its leaves, and like a garden having no water.
verses.1:31: And their strength shall be like a stalk of tow, and their works like sparks, and the lawless and the sinners shall be burned up together, and there shall be no one to quench them.
verses.2:1: The word that came to Isaiah the son of Amoz concerning Judea and concerning Jerusalem.
verses.2:2: For it shall come to pass in the last days that the mountain of the Lord shall be manifest, and the house of God upon the summit of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills, and all the nations shall come to it.
verses.2:3: And many nations shall go and say, "Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob, and He will declare His way to us, and we shall walk in it." For out of Zion law shall go forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
verses.2:4: And He shall judge between the nations and reprove a great people; and they shall beat their swords into plows and their spears into sickles, and nation shall not take up a sword against nation, nor shall they learn to wage war anymore.
verses.2:5: And now, O house of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the Lord.
verses.2:6: For He has forsaken His people, the house of Israel, because their country has been filled as from the beginning with divinations, like that of the foreigners, and many foreign children have been born to them.
verses.2:7: For their country was filled with silver and gold, and there was no number to their treasures; and the land was filled with horses, and there was no number to their chariots;
verses.2:8: and the land was filled with abominations, the works of their hands, and they worshiped what their fingers made.
verses.2:9: And mankind bowed down, and man was humbled, and I will by no means forgive them.
verses.2:10: And now enter into the rocks and hide yourselves in the earth from the presence of the dread of the Lord and from the glory of His might, when He arises to shatter the earth.
verses.2:11: For the eyes of the Lord are lofty, while man is lowly; and the loftiness of men shall be humbled, and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.
verses.2:12: For the day of the Lord of hosts is upon every insolent and proud one, and upon every lofty and towering one, and they shall be humbled,
verses.2:13: and upon every cedar of Lebanon among the lofty and towering, and upon every oak tree of Bashan,
verses.2:14: and upon every mountain, and upon every high hill,
verses.2:15: and upon every high tower, and upon every high wall,
verses.2:16: and upon every ship of the sea, and upon every sight of ships of beauty.
verses.2:17: And every man shall be humbled, and the arrogance of men shall fall, and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.
verses.2:18: And all the things made by hands they shall hide away,
verses.2:19: carrying them into the caves, and into the clefts of the rocks, and into the holes of the earth, from the presence of the dread of the Lord and from the glory of His might, when He arises to shatter the earth.
verses.2:20: For in that day a man shall cast out his abominations of silver and gold, which they made to worship, to the vain things and to the bats,
verses.2:21: in order to enter into the holes of the solid rock and into the clefts of the rocks, from the presence of the dread of the Lord and from the glory of His might, when He arises to shatter the earth.
verses.3:1: Behold now, the Sovereign Lord of hosts will remove from Jerusalem and from Judea the strong man and the strong woman, the strength of bread and the strength of water,
verses.3:2: the giant and the strong man and the man of war, and the judge and the prophet and the diviner and the elder,
verses.3:3: and the captain of fifty and the admirable counselor, and the wise master builder and the discerning hearer.
verses.3:4: And I will appoint youths as their rulers, and mockers shall have dominion over them.
verses.3:5: And the people will fall upon one another, man against man, and man against his neighbor; the child will strike against the aged man, the dishonorable against the honorable.
verses.3:6: For a man will take hold of his brother or of a kinsman of his father, saying, "You have a garment; become our leader, and let my food be under you."
verses.3:7: And answering, he will say in that day, "I will not be your leader, for in my house there is neither bread nor garment; I will not be a leader of this people."
verses.3:8: For Jerusalem has been forsaken and Judea has fallen, and their tongues are joined with lawlessness, disobeying what pertains to the Lord; therefore now their glory has been brought low,
verses.3:9: and the shame of their countenance has stood against them; and they have declared their sin like that of Sodom and made it manifest. Woe to their soul, for they have devised an evil counsel against themselves,
verses.3:10: saying, "Let us bind the righteous one, because he is burdensome to us." Therefore they shall eat the produce of their works.
verses.3:11: Woe to the lawless one! Evil things shall befall him according to the works of his hands.
verses.3:12: O My people, your exactors glean you, and those who demand payment have dominion over you. O My people, those who call you blessed lead you astray and trouble the path of your feet.
verses.3:13: But now the Lord will rise up for judgment, and He will bring His people to stand for judgment;
verses.3:14: the Lord Himself will come into judgment with the elders of the people and with its rulers: "And why have you burned up My vineyard, and why is the plunder of the poor in your houses?
verses.3:15: Why do you wrong My people, and put the countenance of the poor to shame?"
verses.3:16: Thus says the Lord: "Because the daughters of Zion have been lifted up, and have walked with a lofty neck and with winking of the eyes, and in the gait of their feet trailing their tunics as they go, and sporting with their feet at the same time,
verses.3:17: God will therefore humble the ruling daughters of Zion, and the Lord will uncover their form
verses.3:18: in that day; and the Lord will take away the glory of their apparel: the braided ornaments and the tassels and the crescents,
verses.3:19: and the pendant and the ornament of their face,
verses.3:20: and the array of glorious adornment, and the bangles and the bracelets and the hair clasp and the finger rings and the armbands and the earrings,
verses.3:21: and the purple-bordered robes and the purple-woven garments,
verses.3:22: and the wraps worn about the house and the transparent Laconian garments,
verses.3:23: and the fine linens and the blue and scarlet garments, and the fine linen interwoven with gold and blue, and the flowing summer veils.
verses.3:24: And instead of sweet fragrance there shall be dust; and instead of a sash you shall gird yourself with a rope; and instead of the golden ornament of the head you shall have baldness because of your works; and instead of the purple-woven tunic you shall gird yourself with sackcloth.
verses.3:25: And your fairest son, whom you love, shall fall by the sword, and your strong men shall fall by the sword and be brought low;
verses.3:26: and the cases of your adornment shall mourn, and you shall be left alone and be leveled to the ground."
verses.4:1: And seven women shall take hold of one man, saying, "We will eat our own bread, and we will put on our own garments; only let your name be called upon us—take away our reproach."
verses.4:2: And in that day God shall shine forth in counsel with glory upon the earth, to exalt and glorify the remnant of Israel;
verses.4:3: and it shall come to pass that what is left behind in Zion and what remains in Jerusalem—they shall be called holy, all who have been written for life in Jerusalem;
verses.4:4: for the Lord will wash away the filth of the sons and of the daughters of Zion, and He will cleanse the blood from their midst by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.
verses.4:5: And He will come, and it shall be that a cloud will overshadow every place of Mount Zion and all that is around her by day, and as of smoke and the light of a burning fire by night; and with all glory it shall be sheltered;
verses.4:6: and it shall be for a shade from the heat, and for a shelter and a hiding place from harshness and rain.
verses.5:1: Now I will sing to the Beloved a song of my Beloved concerning my vineyard. A vineyard belonged to the Beloved on a horn, in a fertile place.
verses.5:2: And I placed a hedge around it and fenced it in, and I planted a Sorek vine, and I built a tower in its midst, and I dug a winepress vat in it; and I waited for it to bring forth grapes, and it brought forth thorns.
verses.5:3: And now, you who dwell in Jerusalem and man of Judah, judge between Me and My vineyard.
verses.5:4: What more shall I do for My vineyard that I have not done for it? Because I waited for it to bring forth grapes, yet it brought forth thorns.
verses.5:5: And now I will declare to you what I will do to My vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it shall be for plunder; and I will tear down its wall, and it shall be for trampling underfoot.
verses.5:6: And I will forsake My vineyard, and it shall neither be pruned nor dug, and thorns shall spring up upon it as upon dry wasteland; and I will command the clouds not to send rain upon it.
verses.5:7: For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel, and the man of Judah is a beloved young plant; I waited for it to execute justice, yet it practiced lawlessness, and not righteousness, but an outcry.
verses.5:8: Woe to those who join house to house and bring field near to field, that they may take something away from their neighbor! Shall you dwell alone upon the earth?
verses.5:9: For these things have been heard in the ears of the Lord of hosts: for even if many houses come to be, they shall become a desolation—great and fair—and there shall be none dwelling in them.
verses.5:10: For where ten yokes of oxen labor, it shall yield one jar, and he who sows six artabas shall yield three measures.
verses.5:11: Woe to those who rise early in the morning and pursue strong drink, who linger late into the evening; for wine shall inflame them.
verses.5:12: For with lyre and harp, and timbrels and flutes, they drink wine, yet they do not regard the works of the Lord, nor do they consider the works of His hands.
verses.5:13: Therefore My people have become captive because they do not know the Lord, and a multitude of the dead has come to be because of famine and thirst for water.
verses.5:14: And Hades has enlarged its soul and opened wide its mouth without ceasing; and her glorious ones and her great ones and her rich ones and her pestilent ones shall descend.
verses.5:15: And mankind shall be humbled, and man shall be dishonored, and the lofty eyes shall be brought low;
verses.5:16: and the Lord of hosts shall be exalted in judgment, and the holy God shall be glorified in righteousness;
verses.5:17: and those who were plundered shall graze like bulls, and lambs shall eat the desolate places of those who were taken away.
verses.5:18: Woe to those who draw sins to themselves as with a long rope, and lawless deeds as with the yoke strap of a heifer,
verses.5:19: who say, "Let what He will do draw near with speed, that we may see, and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel come, that we may know!"
verses.5:20: Woe to those who declare evil to be good and good to be evil, who make darkness light and light darkness, who make bitter sweet and sweet bitter.
verses.5:21: Woe to those who are prudent in themselves, and knowledgeable in their own sight.
verses.5:22: Woe to the strong ones among you who drink wine, and the mighty men who mingle strong drink,
verses.5:23: who justify the ungodly for the sake of bribes, and take away the right of the righteous.
verses.5:24: Therefore, just as stubble shall be burned by a coal of fire and consumed by an unrestrained flame, so their root shall be like chaff, and their blossom shall rise up like dust; for they did not desire the law of the Lord of hosts, but provoked the oracle of the Holy One of Israel.
verses.5:25: And the Lord of hosts was incensed with wrath against His people, and He laid His hand upon them and struck them; and the mountains were provoked, and their carcasses became like refuse in the midst of the road. Yet for all this His fury was not turned away, but His hand is still raised high.
verses.5:26: Therefore He will lift up a signal among the nations that are afar off, and He will whistle for them from the end of the earth; and behold, swiftly and lightly they come.
verses.5:27: They shall neither hunger nor grow weary, neither shall they slumber nor sleep; neither shall they loosen their belts from their loins, nor shall the straps of their sandals be broken;
verses.5:28: whose arrows are sharp, and their bows are strung. The feet of their horses are like solid rock; the wheels of their chariots have been reckoned like a tempest.
verses.5:29: They rage like lions, they have taken their stand like a lion's whelps; and he will seize, and cry out like a wild beast, and cast them out, and there shall be none to deliver them,
verses.5:30: and he will roar on their account in that day like the sound of a surging sea; and they shall look to the earth, and behold, harsh darkness in their perplexity.
verses.6:1: And it came to pass in the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated upon a high and exalted throne, and the house was full of His glory.
verses.6:2: And seraphim stood around Him: one had six wings, and another had six wings; with two they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
verses.6:3: And one cried out to another and they said, "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord Sabaoth; all the earth is full of His glory."
verses.6:4: And the lintel was lifted up at the voice with which they cried out, and the house was filled with smoke.
verses.6:5: And I said, "Alas, wretched am I, for I am stunned; for being a man and having unclean lips, I dwell in the midst of a people having unclean lips, and I have seen the King, the Lord Sabaoth, with my eyes."
verses.6:6: And one of the seraphim was sent to me, and in his hand he held a burning coal, which he had taken with the tongs from the altar.
verses.6:7: And he touched my mouth and said, "Behold, this has touched your lips; it shall take away your iniquities, and thoroughly cleanse your sins."
verses.6:8: And I heard the voice of the Lord saying, "Whom shall I send, and who will go to this people?" And I said, "Behold, here I am; send me."
verses.6:9: And He said, "Go and say to this people, 'Hearing you shall hear and shall by no means understand, and seeing you shall see and shall by no means perceive.'
verses.6:10: For the heart of this people has grown thick, and with their ears they have heard heavily, and they have shut their eyes, lest they should ever see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart and turn back, and I should heal them."
verses.6:11: And I said, "How long, O Lord?" And He said, "Until cities are made desolate because they are not inhabited, and houses because there are no people, and the land shall be left desolate.
verses.6:12: And after these things God shall remove the people far away, and those who are left shall be multiplied upon the land.
verses.6:13: And yet a tenth part remains upon it, and again it shall be for plunder, like a terebinth and like an acorn when it falls out of its husk."
verses.7:1: And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin king of Aram and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up against Jerusalem to make war against it, and they were not able to besiege it.
verses.7:2: And it was reported to the house of David, saying, "Aram has come to an agreement with Ephraim." And his soul and the soul of his people were dismayed, just as a tree in a forest is shaken by the wind.
verses.7:3: And the Lord said to Isaiah, "Go out to meet Ahaz, you and your son Jashub who is left, to the pool of the upper road of the fuller's field.
verses.7:4: And you shall say to him, 'Take heed to be quiet and do not fear, nor let your soul grow faint because of these two pieces of wood, these smoking firebrands; for when the wrath of My anger comes, I shall heal again.
verses.7:5: And as for the son of Aram and the son of Remaliah, because they have devised an evil counsel:
verses.7:6: "We will go up into Judea, and having conferred with them we will turn them to ourselves, and we will make the son of Tabeel king over it"—
verses.7:7: thus says the Lord Sabaoth: This counsel shall by no means abide, nor shall it come to pass.
verses.7:8: Rather, the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; yet within sixty-five years the kingdom of Ephraim shall cease from being a people.
verses.7:9: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. And if you do not believe, neither shall you understand.'"
verses.7:10: And the Lord spoke again to Ahaz, saying,
verses.7:11: "Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, in the depth or in the height."
verses.7:12: And Ahaz said, "I will by no means ask, nor will I test the Lord."
verses.7:13: And he said, "Hear now, O house of David: Is it a small thing for you to cause a struggle for men, and how is it that you cause a struggle for the Lord?
verses.7:14: Therefore the Lord Himself shall give you a sign: behold, the virgin shall conceive in the womb and bring forth a son, and you shall call His name Immanuel.
verses.7:15: Butter and honey He shall eat before He knows or prefers evil, to choose the good;
verses.7:16: for before the child knows good or evil, He refuses wickedness to choose the good, and the land which you dread before the two kings shall be forsaken.
verses.7:17: Yet God shall bring upon you, and upon your people, and upon your father's house, days that have not yet come since the day that He removed Ephraim from Judah—even the king of the Assyrians."
verses.7:18: And it shall come to pass in that day that the Lord shall whistle for flies, which shall rule over part of the river of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of the Assyrians;
verses.7:19: and they shall all come into the ravines of the land, and into the clefts of the rocks, and into the caves, and into every crevice.
verses.7:20: In that day the Lord shall shave the head and the hair of the feet with the hired razor from beyond the river of the king of the Assyrians, and He shall take away the beard.
verses.7:21: And it shall come to pass in that day that a man shall rear a heifer of the herd and two sheep;
verses.7:22: and it shall come to pass, from producing abundant milk, everyone who is left upon the land shall eat butter and honey.
verses.7:23: And it shall come to pass in that day that every place where there are a thousand vines worth a thousand shekels shall become barren ground and thorns.
verses.7:24: With arrow and bow they shall enter there, for all the land shall be barren ground and thorns.
verses.7:25: And every mountain that is plowed shall surely be plowed; fear shall by no means come there, for from the barren ground and thorns it shall become a pasture for sheep and a trampling place for oxen.
verses.8:1: And the Lord said to me, "Take for yourself a great new scroll, and write upon it with a man's stylus concerning swiftly making a plunder of spoils, for it is at hand;
verses.8:2: and make faithful men witnesses for Me: Uriah, and Zechariah the son of Berechiah."
verses.8:3: And I approached the prophetess, and she conceived in the womb and bore a son. And the Lord said to me, "Call his name 'Quickly Spoil, Swiftly Plunder';
verses.8:4: for before the child knows how to call out father or mother, he shall take the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria before the king of the Assyrians."
verses.8:5: And the Lord continued speaking to me yet again:
verses.8:6: "Because this people does not desire the water of Siloam that flows gently, but desires to have Rezin and the son of Remaliah as king over you,
verses.8:7: therefore, behold, the Lord brings up upon you the water of the river, mighty and abundant, even the king of the Assyrians and his glory; and he shall come up over every ravine of yours, and shall walk over every wall of yours,
verses.8:8: and he shall remove from Judea any man who is able to lift up his head or capable of accomplishing anything; and his encampment shall be so as to fill the breadth of your land." God is with us.
verses.8:9: Know, O nations, and be defeated; give ear, even to the farthest part of the earth; though you have grown strong, be defeated; for if you grow strong again, again you shall be defeated.
verses.8:10: And whatever counsel you may devise, the Lord shall scatter it; and the word which you speak shall by no means abide among you, for God is with us.
verses.8:11: Thus says the Lord: "With a strong hand they refuse the course of the way of this people, saying,
verses.8:12: 'Let them never say what is hard; for everything that this people says is hard; and you shall by no means fear its fear, nor be troubled.
verses.8:13: Sanctify the Lord Himself, and He shall be your fear.'
verses.8:14: And if you trust in Him, He shall be to you a sanctuary, and you shall not encounter Him as a stone of stumbling, nor as a rock of falling. But the houses of Jacob are in a snare, and those dwelling in Jerusalem are in a hollow pit;
verses.8:15: therefore many among them shall grow weak, and they shall fall and be crushed, and men living in security shall draw near and be captured."
verses.8:16: Then those who seal up the law so as not to learn shall be made manifest.
verses.8:17: And he shall say, "I will wait for God, who has turned away His face from the house of Jacob, and I will trust in Him.
verses.8:18: Behold, I and the children whom God has given me. And they shall be signs and wonders in the house of Israel from the Lord Sabaoth, who dwells on Mount Zion."
verses.8:19: And if they say to you, "Seek the mediums, and those who call out from the earth, those who speak empty words, who voice sounds out of their belly"—shall not a nation seek after its God? Why do they seek the dead on behalf of the living?
verses.8:20: For He gave the law for help, that they might speak not according to this word, concerning which there are no gifts to give for it.
verses.8:21: And a severe famine shall come upon you; and it shall come to pass, when you grow hungry, you shall be grieved and shall speak evil of the ruler and the ancestral traditions; and they shall look up to heaven above,
verses.8:22: and they shall gaze upon the earth below; and behold, dire perplexity and darkness, affliction and anguish and darkness so as not to see; and the one who is in anguish shall not be at a loss until a season.
verses.8:23: Drink this first, act swiftly, O region of Zebulun, the land of Naphtali, and the rest along the seacoast and beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
verses.9:1: O people who walk in darkness, behold a great light; you who dwell in a region of the shadow of death, light shall shine upon you.
verses.9:2: The greater part of the people whom You brought down in Your gladness—they shall indeed rejoice before You as those who rejoice at the harvest, and in the same manner as those who divide the spoil.
verses.9:3: Because the yoke resting upon them has been removed, and the rod upon their neck; for He has shattered the rod of the exactors, as in the day against Midian.
verses.9:4: For every robe amassed by deceit, and every garment, they shall repay with restitution, and they shall wish that they had been burned with fire.
verses.9:5: For a Child has been born to us, a Son has been given to us, whose dominion has come upon His shoulder, and His name is called Messenger of Great Counsel; for I will bring peace upon the rulers, and health to Him.
verses.9:6: Great is His dominion, and of His peace there is no limit, upon the throne of David and his kingdom, to set it aright and uphold it with judgment and with righteousness, from this time forth and forevermore. The zeal of the Lord of hosts shall accomplish these things.
verses.9:7: The Lord sent death upon Jacob, and it came upon Israel.
verses.9:8: And all the people of Ephraim shall know, and those who dwell in Samaria, saying in insolence and loftiness of heart:
verses.9:9: "Bricks have fallen, but come, let us hew stones, and cut down sycamores and cedars, and build for ourselves a tower."
verses.9:10: And God shall dash upon him those who rise up against Mount Zion, and He shall scatter the enemies,
verses.9:11: Syria from the rising of the sun and the Greeks from the setting of the sun, who devour Israel with their whole mouth. For all these things His wrath has not turned away, but His hand is still raised high.
verses.9:12: And the people did not turn back until they were struck, and they did not seek the Lord.
verses.9:13: And the Lord took away from Israel head and tail, great and small in one day: the elder and those who respect persons, this is the leadership,
verses.9:14: and the prophet who teaches lawless things, he is the tail.
verses.9:15: And those who call this people blessed shall lead them astray, and they lead them astray in order to swallow them up.
verses.9:16: Therefore the Lord shall not rejoice over their young men, and He shall have no mercy on their orphans and their widows; for all are lawless and wicked, and every mouth speaks unjust things. For all these things His wrath has not turned away, but His hand is still raised high.
verses.9:17: And lawlessness shall burn like fire, and like dry grass it shall be devoured by fire; and it shall burn in the thickets of the forest, and consume together all that surrounds the hills.
verses.9:18: Because of the fury of the wrath of the Lord the whole land has been burned up, and the people shall be as though burned up by fire. A man shall not have pity on his brother,
verses.9:19: but he shall turn aside to the right, because he shall be hungry, and he shall eat from the left, and a man shall by no means be filled, eating the flesh of his own arm.
verses.9:20: For Manasseh shall eat of Ephraim, and Ephraim of Manasseh, for together they shall besiege Judah. For all these things His wrath has not turned away, but His hand is still raised high.
verses.10:1: Woe to those who write wickedness; for in writing, they write wickedness,
verses.10:2: turning aside the justice of the poor, snatching away the judgment of the needy of My people, so that the widow becomes their plunder and the orphan their spoil.
verses.10:3: And what shall they do in the day of visitation? For affliction shall come upon you from afar. And to whom shall you flee to be helped? And where shall you leave your glory, lest you fall into captivity?
verses.10:4: For all these things His anger has not turned away, but His hand is still raised high.
verses.10:5: Woe to the Assyrians! The rod of My wrath and anger is in their hands.
verses.10:6: I will send My anger against a lawless nation, and I will command My people to take spoil and plunder, and to trample down the cities and turn them into dust.
verses.10:7: Yet he did not intend it thus, nor has he reasoned thus in his soul; rather, his mind shall change, even to utterly destroy nations not a few.
verses.10:8: And if they say to him, "You alone are ruler,"
verses.10:9: then he shall say, "Did I not capture the region above Babylon and Calneh, where the tower was built? And I captured Arabia, and Damascus, and Samaria.
verses.10:10: In the same manner as I captured these, I shall also capture all the realms. Wail, you carved images in Jerusalem and in Samaria;
verses.10:11: for just as I did to Samaria and her hand-made images, so I shall also do to Jerusalem and her idols."
verses.10:12: And it shall come to pass, when the Lord finishes doing all things on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, He shall bring judgment upon the haughty mind, upon the ruler of the Assyrians, and upon the loftiness of the glory of his eyes.
verses.10:13: For he said, "By strength I shall act, and by the wisdom of understanding I shall remove the boundaries of nations, and their strength I shall plunder;
verses.10:14: and I shall shake inhabited cities, and I shall seize the whole inhabited world in my hand like a nest, and like forsaken eggs I shall take them up; and there is none who shall escape me or speak against me."
verses.10:15: Shall an axe be glorified without the one who chops with it? Or shall a saw be exalted without the one who pulls it? Just as when one lifts a rod or a wooden staff—and is it not so?
verses.10:16: Rather, the Lord of hosts shall send dishonor upon your honor, and upon your glory a burning fire shall burn;
verses.10:17: and the Light of Israel shall become a fire, and He shall sanctify him in a burning fire, and it shall devour the woodland like grass.
verses.10:18: In that day the mountains and the hills and the forests shall be extinguished, and it shall devour from soul even to flesh; and the one who flees shall be like one fleeing from a burning flame.
verses.10:19: And those who remain of them shall be a mere number, and a little child shall write them down.
verses.10:20: And it shall come to pass in that day that the remnant of Israel shall no longer be added to, and those of Jacob who have been saved shall by no means trust any longer in those who wronged them, but they shall trust in God, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.
verses.10:21: And the remnant of Jacob shall rest upon the mighty God.
verses.10:22: And though the people of Israel become like the sand of the sea, the remnant of them shall be saved;
verses.10:23: bringing a word to completion and cutting it short in righteousness, because the Lord shall execute a shortened word in the whole inhabited world.
verses.10:24: Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts: "Do not be afraid, My people, you who dwell in Zion, of the Assyrians, because he shall strike you with a rod; for I am bringing a blow upon you, to see the way of Egypt.
verses.10:25: For yet a little while and the anger shall cease, and My wrath shall be against their counsel."
verses.10:26: And God shall rouse Himself against them according to the blow of Midian in a place of affliction, and His wrath shall be on the way by the sea, toward the way to Egypt.
verses.10:27: And it shall come to pass in that day that his yoke shall be removed from your shoulder, and the fear of him from you, and the yoke shall be destroyed from your shoulders.
verses.10:28: For he shall come to the city of Aggai, and he shall pass on to Megiddo, and in Michmash he shall deposit his baggage;
verses.10:29: and he shall pass through a ravine and come to Aggai; fear shall seize Ramah, the city of Saul. She shall flee—
verses.10:30: the daughter of Gallim; she shall hear in Sa, she shall hear in Anathoth.
verses.10:31: And Madmenah is dismayed, and those who dwell in Gibbeir.
verses.10:32: Exhort today to remain on the way; with the hand beckon to the mountain, the daughter of Zion, and you hills that are in Jerusalem.
verses.10:33: Behold, the Sovereign, the Lord of hosts, confounds the glorious ones with might, and those who are lofty in arrogance shall be crushed, and the lofty shall be brought low,
verses.10:34: and the lofty shall fall by the sword, and Lebanon shall fall together with the lofty ones.
verses.11:1: And a Rod shall come forth from the root of Jesse, and a Blossom shall spring up from the root.
verses.11:2: And the Spirit of God shall rest upon Him, the Spirit of wisdom and understanding, the Spirit of counsel and strength, the Spirit of knowledge and godliness;
verses.11:3: the Spirit of the fear of God shall fill Him. He shall not judge according to outward appearance, nor shall He reprove according to report;
verses.11:4: but He shall render judgment for the humble, and He shall reprove the lowly of the earth; and He shall strike the earth with the word of His mouth, and with the breath through His lips He shall slay the ungodly.
verses.11:5: And He shall have His loins girded with righteousness, and His sides wrapped with truth.
verses.11:6: And the wolf shall pasture with the lamb, and the leopard shall rest with the kid, and the calf and the bull and the lion shall graze together, and a little child shall lead them.
verses.11:7: And the cow and the bear shall pasture together, and their young shall be together; and the lion, like the ox, shall eat straw.
verses.11:8: And an infant child shall lay his hand upon the holes of asps, and upon the den of the offspring of asps.
verses.11:9: And they shall by no means do harm, nor shall they be able to destroy anyone upon My holy mountain; for the whole earth has been filled with knowing the Lord, as abundant water covers the seas.
verses.11:10: And in that day there shall be the Root of Jesse, and He who rises up to rule over the nations; in Him the nations shall hope, and His rest shall be honor.
verses.11:11: And it shall come to pass in that day that the Lord shall yet again show His hand to be zealous for the remaining remnant of the people, that which is left by the Assyrians, and from Egypt, and from Babylonia, and Ethiopia, and from the Elamites, and from the rising of the sun, and from Arabia.
verses.11:12: And He shall lift up a standard to the nations, and He shall gather the lost ones of Israel, and the dispersed of Judah He shall gather from the four wings of the earth.
verses.11:13: And the jealousy of Ephraim shall be taken away, and the enemies of Judah shall perish; Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not afflict Ephraim.
verses.11:14: And they shall fly in the ships of foreigners; together they shall plunder the sea, and those from the rising of the sun, and Idumea; and upon Moab first they shall lay their hands, and the sons of Ammon shall be the first to obey.
verses.11:15: And the Lord shall make desolate the sea of Egypt, and He shall lay His hand upon the river with a violent wind, and He shall strike seven channels so that one may cross it in sandals;
verses.11:16: and there shall be a passage for My people who remain in Egypt, and it shall be for Israel like the day when he came out from the land of Egypt.
verses.12:1: And in that day you shall say, "I bless You, O Lord, because You were angry with me, and You turned away Your wrath and had mercy on me.
verses.12:2: Behold, my God is my Savior; I will trust in Him and will not be afraid, for the Lord is my glory and my praise, and He has become my salvation."
verses.12:3: And you shall draw water with gladness from the springs of salvation.
verses.12:4: And in that day you shall say, "Sing hymns to the Lord, call aloud upon His name, declare His glorious deeds among the nations; remember that His name has been exalted.
verses.12:5: Sing hymns to the name of the Lord, for He has done lofty things; proclaim these things in all the earth.
verses.12:6: Exult and be glad, you who dwell in Zion, for the Holy One of Israel has been exalted in her midst."
verses.13:1: The vision which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw against Babylon.
verses.13:2: Upon a level mountain lift up a banner, raise the voice to them, beckon with the hand; open, O rulers!
verses.13:3: I command them, even I; giants are coming to fulfill My wrath, both rejoicing and acting with insolence.
verses.13:4: The sound of many nations upon the mountains, like that of many nations, the sound of kings and of nations gathered together! The Lord of hosts has commanded an armed warrior nation
verses.13:5: to come from a land far away, from the farthest foundation of heaven—the Lord and His armed warriors—to utterly destroy the whole inhabited earth.
verses.13:6: Wail! For the day of the Lord is near, and destruction from God shall come.
verses.13:7: Therefore every hand shall grow weak, and every soul of man shall lose heart;
verses.13:8: the ambassadors shall be thrown into turmoil, and birth pangs shall seize them like those of a woman in labor; and they shall lament one to another and be astounded, and their countenance shall change like a flame.
verses.13:9: For behold, the day of the Lord comes, incurable, full of wrath and anger, to make the inhabited earth a desolation and to destroy the sinners from it.
verses.13:10: For the stars of heaven and Orion and all the array of heaven shall not give their light; and it shall be darkened as the sun rises, and the moon shall not give her light.
verses.13:11: And I will command evils upon the whole inhabited earth, and upon the ungodly their sins; and I will destroy the arrogance of the lawless, and I will humble the arrogance of the proud.
verses.13:12: And those who remain shall be more precious than unfired gold, and a man shall be more precious than the stone that is in Souphir.
verses.13:13: For heaven shall be enraged, and the earth shall be shaken from its foundations, because of the fury of the wrath of the Lord of hosts, in the day when His wrath comes.
verses.13:14: And those who remain shall be like a fleeing gazelle and like a wandering sheep, and there shall be no one to gather them, so that each man shall turn back to his own people, and each man shall flee to his own country.
verses.13:15: For whoever is captured shall be overcome, and whoever are gathered together shall fall by the sword.
verses.13:16: And they shall dash their children down before their sight, and they shall plunder their houses, and they shall take their wives.
verses.13:17: Behold, I am stirring up the Medes against you, who do not regard silver, neither do they have need of gold.
verses.13:18: They shall shatter the arrows of the young men, and they shall by no means have mercy on your children, nor shall their eyes spare your children.
verses.13:19: And Babylon, which is called glorious by the king of the Chaldeans, shall be just as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah;
verses.13:20: it shall never be inhabited for all time, neither shall any enter it through many generations, neither shall Arabs pass through it, nor shall shepherds rest in it.
verses.13:21: And wild beasts shall rest there, and the houses shall be filled with noise; and sirens shall rest there, and demons shall dance there,
verses.13:22: and onocentaurs shall dwell there, and hedgehogs shall make their nests in their houses. It comes swiftly and shall not delay.
verses.14:1: And the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and they shall rest upon their own land; and the sojourner shall be joined to them, and shall be joined to the house of Jacob.
verses.14:2: And nations shall take them and bring them into their own place, and they shall inherit, and they shall be multiplied upon the land as menservants and maidservants; and those who took them captive shall become captives, and those who ruled over them shall be ruled over.
verses.14:3: And it shall come to pass in that day that the Lord will give you rest from your pain and your wrath, from your hard bondage in which you served them.
verses.14:4: And you shall take up this lamentation against the king of Babylon, and say: "How has the exactor ceased, and how has the taskmaster ceased?
verses.14:5: The Lord has broken the yoke of the sinners, the yoke of the rulers.
verses.14:6: Having struck a nation in wrath with an incurable blow, smiting a nation with a blow of wrath that did not spare, he has come to rest in confidence.
verses.14:7: All the earth cries aloud with gladness,
verses.14:8: and the trees of Lebanon have rejoiced over you, and the cedar of Lebanon: 'Since you have fallen asleep, the one who cuts us down has not come up.'
verses.14:9: Hades from below was embittered upon meeting you; all the giants who ruled the earth have been roused together for you, who raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.
verses.14:10: All of them shall answer and say to you, 'You also have been captured just as we were, and you have been reckoned among us!'
verses.14:11: Your glory has gone down into Hades, your great gladness; beneath you they shall spread decay, and your covering is the worm.
verses.14:12: How has the morning star, who rises at dawn, fallen from heaven? He who sent to all the nations has been shattered to the earth.
verses.14:13: Yet you said in your mind, 'I will ascend into heaven; above the stars of heaven I will set my throne; I will sit upon a high mountain, upon the high mountains toward the north;
verses.14:14: I will ascend above the clouds; I will be like the Most High.'
verses.14:15: Yet now you shall go down into Hades, even into the foundations of the earth.
verses.14:16: Those who see you shall marvel at you and say, 'This is the man who provoked the earth, who shook kings,
verses.14:17: who made the whole inhabited earth a desolation, and pulled down his cities, who did not release those in captivity.'
verses.14:18: All the kings of the nations have fallen asleep in honor, each man in his own house;
verses.14:19: but you shall be cast out in the mountains, like an abominable corpse, with many dead who were pierced through with swords, going down into Hades.
verses.14:20: Just as a garment stained with blood shall not be clean, so neither shall you be clean, because you have destroyed my land and slain my people; you shall by no means remain for all time, O wicked offspring.
verses.14:21: Prepare your children to be slaughtered for the sins of their father, lest they rise up and inherit the earth and fill the earth with wars."
verses.14:22: "And I will rise up against them," says the Lord of hosts, "and I will destroy their name and remnant and offspring." Thus says the Lord:
verses.14:23: "And I will make Babylonia a desolation so that hedgehogs dwell there, and it shall come to nothing; and I will make it a pit of mire for destruction."
verses.14:24: Thus says the Lord of hosts: "Just as I have spoken, so shall it be, and just as I have purposed, so shall it abide,
verses.14:25: to destroy the Assyrians upon My land and upon My mountains; and they shall be trampled underfoot, and their yoke shall be taken away from them, and their glory shall be removed from their shoulders."
verses.14:26: This is the counsel which the Lord has purposed against the whole inhabited earth, and this is the uplifted hand against all the nations.
verses.14:27: For the things which the holy God has purposed, who shall frustrate? And His uplifted hand, who shall turn back?
verses.14:28: In the year in which King Ahaz died, this word came:
verses.14:29: Do not rejoice, all you foreigners, because the yoke of him who struck you has been broken; for out of the seed of a serpent shall come forth the offspring of asps, and their offspring shall come forth as flying serpents.
verses.14:30: And the poor shall be fed through Him, and poor men shall rest in peace; but He shall slay your offspring with famine, and He shall slay your remnant.
verses.14:31: Wail, O gates of cities! Let the troubled cities cry aloud, all you foreigners! For smoke comes from the north, and there is no way to endure.
verses.14:32: And what shall the kings of the nations answer? "The Lord has founded Zion, and through Him the humble of the people shall be saved."
verses.15:1: The word against the land of Moab. By night the land of Moab shall perish, for by night the wall of the land of Moab shall perish.
verses.15:2: Grieve for yourselves, for Dibon also shall perish, where your altar is; there you shall go up to weep, upon Nebo of the land of Moab. Wail! Upon every head is baldness, and all arms are gashed.
verses.15:3: In her broad squares gird yourselves with sackcloth, and lament upon her housetops and in her streets; all of you wail with weeping.
verses.15:4: For Heshbon and Elealeh have cried out; as far as Jahaz their voice has been heard; therefore the loins of the land of Moab cry out; her soul shall know it.
verses.15:5: The heart of the land of Moab cries out within her as far as Zoar, for she is a heifer of three years old; and by the ascent of Luhith they shall go up to you weeping by the way of Horonaim; destruction and earthquake cry out.
verses.15:6: The water of Nimrim shall be desolate, and her grass shall fail; for there shall be no green grass.
verses.15:7: Even so, shall she be saved? For I will bring Arabians upon the valley, and they shall take it.
verses.15:8: For the outcry has reached the border of the land of Moab, of Eglaim, and her wailing as far as the well of Elim.
verses.15:9: And the water of Dimon shall be filled with blood; for I will bring Arabians upon Dimon, and I will take away the seed of Moab, and Ariel, and the remnant of Admah.
verses.16:1: I will send forth as creeping things upon the earth; is the mountain of the daughter of Zion a desolate rock?
verses.16:2: For you shall be like a nestling taken away from a bird taking flight; you shall be, O daughter of Moab. Upon these things, O Arnon, further
verses.16:3: take counsel; make a shelter of mourning for her continually. In midday darkness they flee; they are dismayed; do not be led away.
verses.16:4: The fugitives of Moab shall sojourn with you; they shall be a shelter to you from the face of the pursuer, for your alliance has been taken away, and the ruler who tramples down has perished from the earth.
verses.16:5: And with mercy a throne shall be set aright, and One shall sit upon it with truth in the tent of David, judging and earnestly seeking judgment and hastening righteousness.
verses.16:6: We have heard of the arrogance of Moab—exceedingly arrogant is he; I have taken away the pride. Not so is your divination, not so.
verses.16:7: Moab shall wail, for in the land of Moab all shall wail; you shall take thought for those who dwell in Deseth, and you shall not be put to shame.
verses.16:8: The plains of Heshbon shall mourn, and the vine of Sibmah; you who swallow up the nations, you shall trample down her vines as far as Jazer. You shall by no means reach them; wander through the wilderness; those who were sent out have been forsaken, for they crossed over the sea.
verses.16:9: Therefore I will weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah; Heshbon and Elealeh have cast down your trees, for upon your harvest and upon your vintage I will trample, and all things shall fall.
verses.16:10: And gladness and exultation shall be taken away from the vineyards; and in your vineyards they shall by no means rejoice, and they shall by no means tread wine into the wine vats, for it has ceased.
verses.16:11: Therefore my inner being shall sound like a harp for Moab, and my inward parts like a wall you have renewed.
verses.16:12: And it shall come to pass that you shall be put to shame, because Moab has grown weary upon the altars; and he shall enter into her handmade shrines to pray, and it shall by no means be able to deliver him.
verses.16:13: This is the word which the Lord spoke concerning Moab when He spoke.
verses.16:14: And now I say, "Within three years, as the years of a hired servant, the glory of Moab shall be dishonored with all that great wealth, and he shall be left very small and without honor."
verses.17:1: The word against Damascus. Behold, Damascus shall be removed from among cities, and shall become a ruin,
verses.17:2: forsaken forever, for a fold of flocks and a resting place, and there shall be none to drive them away;
verses.17:3: and she shall no longer be a stronghold for Ephraim to flee to, and there shall no longer be a kingdom in Damascus nor the remnant of the Syrians; for you are not better than the sons of Israel and their glory. Thus says the Lord of hosts:
verses.17:4: "In that day there shall be a failing of the glory of Jacob, and the fatness of his glory shall be shaken.
verses.17:5: And it shall be as when someone gathers the standing harvest and reaps the seed of the ears of grain; and it shall be as when someone gathers an ear of grain in a hard valley,
verses.17:6: and stubble is left in it, or like two or three olive berries on the lofty tip, or four or five are left upon their branches," thus says the Lord God of Israel.
verses.17:7: In that day a man shall trust in Him who made him, and his eyes shall look upon the Holy One of Israel;
verses.17:8: and they shall by no means trust in the altars, nor in the works of their hands which their fingers have made, and they shall not look upon the trees nor upon their abominations.
verses.17:9: In that day your cities shall be forsaken, just as the Amorites and the Hivites forsook them from before the face of the sons of Israel, and they shall be desolate,
verses.17:10: because you have forsaken God your Savior, and have not remembered the Lord your Helper. Therefore you shall plant an unfaithful planting and an unfaithful seed;
verses.17:11: and on the day that you plant, you shall go astray; and if you sow in the morning, it shall blossom for a harvest on whatever day you take your allotment, and like a human father you shall allot an inheritance to your sons.
verses.17:12: Woe to the multitude of many nations! Like a surging sea, so you shall be troubled, and the back of many nations shall roar like water.
verses.17:13: Like much water are many nations, like much water rushing with violence. And He shall cast him off with contempt, and pursue him far away like the fine chaff of winnowers before the wind, and like the dust of a wheel that a tempest carries away.
verses.17:14: Toward evening, there shall be mourning; before morning, he shall be no more. This is the portion of those who plundered you, and the inheritance for those who inherited you.
verses.18:1: Woe to the wings of ships of the land beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,
verses.18:2: he who sends hostages by sea, and papyrus letters upon the water. For swift messengers shall go to a lofty nation, and to a strange and fierce people; who is beyond it? A nation without hope and trampled down. Now the rivers of the land
verses.18:3: shall all be inhabited like an inhabited country; when their land is lifted up for a signal from a mountain, it shall be heard like the sound of a trumpet.
verses.18:4: For thus the Lord spoke to me: "There shall be security in My city like the light of midday heat, and it shall be like a cloud of dew in the day of harvest."
verses.18:5: Before the harvest, when the blossom is complete, the unripe grape also shall bloom with a sour-grape blossom; and He shall take away the small clusters with pruning hooks, and He shall take away and cut off the vine shoots,
verses.18:6: and He shall leave them together to the birds of heaven and to the wild beasts of the earth; and the birds of heaven shall be gathered together upon them, and all the wild beasts of the earth shall come upon it.
verses.18:7: In that time gifts shall be brought to the Lord of hosts from a people afflicted and plucked, and from a great people from now and forevermore—a nation hoping and trampled down, which is in the region of the river of its land—to the place where the name of the Lord of hosts is, Mount Zion.
verses.19:1: The vision of Egypt. Behold, the Lord sits upon a swift cloud and shall come into Egypt; and the handmade idols of Egypt shall be shaken at His presence, and their heart shall be overcome within them.
verses.19:2: And Egyptians shall rise up against Egyptians, and a man shall make war against his brother, and a man against his neighbor, city against city and district against district.
verses.19:3: And the spirit of the Egyptians shall be troubled within them, and I will scatter their counsel; and they shall inquire of their gods and their images, and those who speak from the earth and the mediums.
verses.19:4: And I will deliver Egypt into the hands of men who are harsh lords, and harsh kings shall rule over them. Thus says the Lord of hosts.
verses.19:5: And the Egyptians shall drink the water that is beside the sea, but the river shall fail and be dried up;
verses.19:6: and the rivers and the canals of the river shall fail, and every gathering of water shall be dried up, even in every marsh of reed and papyrus;
verses.19:7: and all the green sedge around the river, and whatever is sown along the river, shall be dried up, blasted by the wind.
verses.19:8: And the fishermen shall groan, and all who cast hooks into the river shall groan, and those who cast dragnets and the net-casters shall mourn.
verses.19:9: And shame shall seize those who work the combed flax and those who work the fine linen,
verses.19:10: and those who work them shall be in pain, and all who make barley beer shall be grieved and suffer pain in their souls.
verses.19:11: And the rulers of Tanis shall be fools; the wise counselors of the king—their counsel shall be made foolish. How shall you say to the king, "We are sons of men of understanding, sons of kings from the beginning"?
verses.19:12: Where now are your wise men? And let them declare to you and tell what the Lord of hosts has purposed against Egypt.
verses.19:13: The rulers of Tanis have failed, and the rulers of Memphis have been exalted, and they shall lead Egypt astray by tribes.
verses.19:14: For the Lord has mixed for them a spirit of error, and they have led Egypt astray in all their works, as a drunken man staggers while vomiting at the same time.
verses.19:15: And there shall be no work for the Egyptians that shall produce head and tail, and beginning and end.
verses.19:16: And in that day the Egyptians shall be like women, in fear and in trembling before the hand of the Lord of hosts, which He Himself shall lay upon them.
verses.19:17: And the land of the Jews shall become a terror to the Egyptians; whoever mentions it to them, they shall be afraid because of the counsel which the Lord has purposed against it.
verses.19:18: In that day there shall be five cities in Egypt speaking the Canaanite language and swearing by the name of the Lord; one city shall be called the City of Asedek.
verses.19:19: In that day there shall be an altar to the Lord in the land of the Egyptians, and a pillar at its border to the Lord,
verses.19:20: and it shall be for a sign forever to the Lord in the land of Egypt; for they shall cry out to the Lord because of those who afflict them, and He shall send them a man who shall save them; judging, he shall save them.
verses.19:21: And the Lord shall be known to the Egyptians; and the Egyptians shall know the Lord in that day, and they shall offer sacrifices, and they shall make vows to the Lord and fulfill them.
verses.19:22: And the Lord shall strike the Egyptians with a plague, and He shall heal them with healing; and they shall turn back to the Lord, and He shall hear them and heal them.
verses.19:23: In that day there shall be a way from Egypt to the Assyrians, and the Assyrians shall enter into Egypt, and the Egyptians shall go to the Assyrians, and the Egyptians shall serve the Assyrians.
verses.19:24: In that day Israel shall be third among the Egyptians and among the Assyrians, blessed in the land
verses.19:25: which the Lord of hosts has blessed, saying, "Blessed is My people who is in Egypt, and who is among the Assyrians, and the land, My inheritance, Israel."
verses.20:1: In the year when Tanathan entered into Azotus, when he was sent by Arna, king of the Assyrians, and he fought against Azotus and captured it,
verses.20:2: then the Lord spoke to Isaiah the son of Amoz, saying, "Go and remove the sackcloth from your loins, and unfasten your sandals from your feet, and do so, going naked and barefoot."
verses.20:3: And the Lord said, "Just as My servant Isaiah has gone naked and barefoot three years, three years it shall be for signs and wonders to the Egyptians and Ethiopians;
verses.20:4: for thus the king of the Assyrians shall lead away the captivity of Egypt and of the Ethiopians, young men and old men, naked and barefoot together, covered with the shame of Egypt.
verses.20:5: And they shall be put to shame, having been defeated because of the Ethiopians, in whom the Egyptians had trusted, who were their glory.
verses.20:6: And those who dwell on this island shall say in that day, 'Behold, we had trusted to flee to them for help, who were not able to be saved from the king of the Assyrians; and how shall we be saved?'"
verses.21:1: The vision of the wilderness. As a tempest might pass through a wilderness, coming from a wilderness, from a land; a dreadful
verses.21:2: vision and a harsh one has been declared to me. He who breaks faith breaks faith; he who acts lawlessly acts lawlessly. The Elamites are upon me, and the envoys of the Persians come against me. Now I will groan and comfort myself.
verses.21:3: Therefore my loins have been filled with faintness, and pangs have seized me like a woman in travail; I did wrong so as not to hear; I made haste not to see.
verses.21:4: My heart wanders, and lawlessness overwhelms me; my soul stands in fear.
verses.21:5: Prepare the table; eat, drink! Arise, you princes, prepare shields,
verses.21:6: for thus the Lord said to me, "Go, set a watchman for yourself, and declare whatever you see."
verses.21:7: And I saw two mounted horsemen, and a rider of a donkey, and a rider of a camel. Listen with great attention,
verses.21:8: and call Uriah to the watchtower. The Lord said, "I stood continually by day, and at the encampment I stood all the night,
verses.21:9: and behold, he himself comes, a rider of a pair of horses." And he answered and said, "Babylon has fallen, has fallen, and all her statues and her hand-made idols have been shattered to the ground."
verses.21:10: Hear, you who are left behind and you who are in anguish; hear what I have heard from the Lord of hosts: the God of Israel has declared it to us.
verses.21:11: The vision of Idumea. One calls to me from Seir, "Guard the battlements."
verses.21:12: I keep watch in the morning and in the night; if you inquire, inquire, and dwell with me;
verses.21:13: in the forest you shall lodge at evening, in the way of Dedan.
verses.21:14: Bring water to meet the thirsty, you who dwell in the country of Teman; meet those who flee with bread,
verses.21:15: because of the multitude of the slain, and because of the multitude of those who wander, and because of the multitude of the sword, and because of the multitude of the drawn bows, and because of the multitude of those who have fallen in the war.
verses.21:16: For thus the Lord said to me, "Yet a year, like the year of a hired servant, the glory of the sons of Kedar shall fail,
verses.21:17: and the remnant of the bows of the mighty sons of Kedar shall be few." For the Lord God of Israel has spoken.
verses.22:1: The word concerning the Valley of Zion. What has happened to you, that you have all now gone up to vain housetops?
verses.22:2: The city is filled with those who shout; your wounded are not wounded with swords, nor are your dead the dead of war.
verses.22:3: All your rulers have fled, and having been captured they are harshly bound; and the strong among you have fled far away.
verses.22:4: Therefore I said, "Leave me alone; I will weep bitterly. Do not persist in comforting me over the ruin of the daughter of my kindred."
verses.22:5: For it is a day of tumult and destruction, and of trampling and wandering from the Lord of hosts; in the Valley of Zion they wander; from the least to the greatest they wander upon the mountains.
verses.22:6: And the Elamites took up quivers, men riding upon horses, and an assembly in battle array.
verses.22:7: And your choice valleys shall be filled with chariots, and the horsemen shall block up your gates,
verses.22:8: and they shall uncover the gates of Judah; and in that day they shall look upon the choice houses of the city,
verses.22:9: and they shall uncover the hidden places of the houses of the citadel of David. And they saw that they were many, and that he had turned the water of the ancient pool into the city,
verses.22:10: and that they had torn down the houses of Jerusalem for fortifications of the wall for the city.
verses.22:11: And you made for yourselves water between the two walls, inward from the ancient pool; yet you did not look to Him who made it from the beginning, nor did you see Him who created it.
verses.22:12: And the Lord, the Lord of hosts, called in that day for weeping and lamentation, and for shaving the head and girding with sackcloth;
verses.22:13: but they made gladness and exultation, slaughtering calves and sacrificing sheep, so as to eat flesh and drink wine: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die."
verses.22:14: And these things have been revealed in the ears of the Lord of hosts, that this sin shall not be forgiven you until you die.
verses.22:15: Thus says the Lord of hosts: "Go into the treasury chamber to Shebna the treasurer, and say to him,
verses.22:16: 'What are you doing here, and what do you have here, that you have hewn out a tomb for yourself here, and made a tomb for yourself on high, and carved a dwelling for yourself in the rock?
verses.22:17: Behold now, the Lord of hosts casts out and will crush a man, and He will take away your robe and your glorious crown,
verses.22:18: and He will cast you into a great and measureless land, and there you shall die; and He will bring your fine chariot to dishonor, and the house of your ruler,
verses.22:19: and you shall be removed from your stewardship and from your station.
verses.22:20: And it shall come to pass in that day that I will call My servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah,
verses.22:21: and I will clothe him with your robe, and your crown I will give to him with power, and your stewardship I will give into his hands; and he shall be as a father to those who dwell in Jerusalem and to those who dwell in Judah.
verses.22:22: And I will give the glory of David to him, and he shall rule, and there shall be no one who speaks against him; and he shall shut, and there is no one who opens.
verses.22:23: And I will establish him as a ruler in a faithful place, and he shall become a throne of glory for his father's house.
verses.22:24: And every glorious one in his father's house shall trust in him, from the least to the greatest, and they shall hang upon him
verses.22:25: in that day.'" Thus says the Lord of hosts: "The man who is firmly fixed in a faithful place shall be moved, and he shall be taken away and fall, and the glory that is upon him shall be utterly destroyed." For the Lord has spoken.
verses.23:1: The word concerning Tyre. Wail, O ships of Carthage, for she has perished, and they no longer come from the land of Kittim; she has been led away captive.
verses.23:2: To whom have those who dwell in the island become like, merchants of Phoenicia, crossing over the sea
verses.23:3: upon much water, a seed of merchants? Like a harvest being gathered in are the merchants of the nations.
verses.23:4: "Be ashamed, O Sidon," said the sea; and the strength of the sea said, "I have not travailed, nor have I given birth; neither have I reared young men, nor brought up virgins."
verses.23:5: And when it is heard by Egypt, anguish shall seize them concerning Tyre.
verses.23:6: Depart to Carthage; wail, you who dwell in this island.
verses.23:7: Was this not your arrogance from the beginning, before she was delivered up?
verses.23:8: Who has purposed these things against Tyre? Is she inferior, or does she lack strength? Her merchants are glorious, rulers of the earth.
verses.23:9: The Lord of hosts has purposed to dissolve all the arrogance of the glorious, and to bring to dishonor every glorious thing upon the earth.
verses.23:10: Till your land, for ships no longer come from Carthage.
verses.23:11: And your hand no longer prevails over the sea, the hand that provoked kings; the Lord of hosts has commanded concerning Canaan to destroy her strength.
verses.23:12: And they shall say, "You shall no longer continue to insult and wrong the daughter of Sidon; and even if you depart to the Kittim, not even there shall there be rest for you,
verses.23:13: and even to the land of the Chaldeans—this too has been laid waste by the Assyrians; its wall has fallen."
verses.23:14: Wail, O ships of Carthage, for your stronghold has perished.
verses.23:15: And it shall come to pass in that day that Tyre shall be forsaken seventy years, like the time of a king, like the time of a man; and it shall come to pass after seventy years that Tyre shall be like the song of a harlot:
verses.23:16: "Take a harp, wander about, O forgotten harlot city; play the harp skillfully, sing many songs, that remembrance may be made of you."
verses.23:17: And it shall come to pass after the seventy years that God will make a visitation upon Tyre, and she shall again be restored to her former state, and she shall be a marketplace for all the kingdoms of the inhabited world upon the face of the earth.
verses.23:18: And her merchandise and her hire shall be holy to the Lord; it shall not be gathered for themselves, but all her merchandise shall be for those who dwell before the Lord, to eat and drink and be filled, and for a memorial contribution before the Lord.
verses.24:1: Behold, the Lord destroys the inhabited world, and He shall lay it waste, and uncover its face, and scatter those who dwell in it.
verses.24:2: And the people shall be as the priest, and the servant as the master, and the maidservant as the mistress; the buyer shall be as the seller, the lender as the borrower, and the debtor as the one to whom he owes.
verses.24:3: With destruction the earth shall be destroyed, and with plunder the earth shall be plundered; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things.
verses.24:4: The earth mourned, and the inhabited world was ruined; the lofty ones of the earth mourned.
verses.24:5: Moreover, the earth acted lawlessly because of those who inhabit it, because they transgressed the law and altered the ordinances, an everlasting covenant.
verses.24:6: Therefore a curse shall devour the earth, because those who inhabit it have sinned; therefore those who dwell in the earth shall be poor, and few men shall be left.
verses.24:7: The wine shall mourn, the vine shall mourn; all who are glad in soul shall groan.
verses.24:8: The gladness of timbrels has ceased, the arrogance and wealth of the ungodly have ceased, the sound of the harp has ceased.
verses.24:9: They were put to shame; they did not drink wine; strong drink became bitter to those who drink it.
verses.24:10: Every city has been made desolate; one shall shut up a house so that no one may enter.
verses.24:11: Wail for the wine everywhere; all gladness has ceased.
verses.24:12: Cities shall be left desolate, and forsaken houses shall perish.
verses.24:13: All these things shall be in the earth in the midst of the nations: just as when one gleans an olive tree, so shall they glean them, and when the vintage has ceased.
verses.24:14: These shall call out with a shout, and those who are left upon the earth shall rejoice together in the glory of the Lord; the water of the sea shall be troubled.
verses.24:15: Therefore the glory of the Lord shall be in the islands of the sea; the name of the Lord shall be glorious.
verses.24:16: O Lord God of Israel, from the wings of the earth we have heard wonders: "Hope for the godly!" And they shall say, "Woe to the treacherous!" You who set aside the law,
verses.24:17: terror and the pit and the snare are upon you who dwell upon the earth.
verses.24:18: And it shall be that he who flees from the terror shall fall into the pit, and he who climbs out of the pit shall be caught by the snare; for windows from heaven have been opened, and the foundations of the earth shall be shaken.
verses.24:19: With turmoil the earth shall be thrown into turmoil, and with perplexity the earth shall be perplexed.
verses.24:20: The earth has tottered like a drunken and reeling man, and it shall be shaken like an orchard watch-hut; for lawlessness has prevailed upon it, and it shall fall and shall by no means be able to rise.
verses.24:21: And God shall bring His hand upon the host of heaven and upon the kings of the earth.
verses.24:22: And they shall gather its assembly into a prison and shut them up in a stronghold; after many generations there shall be a visitation of them.
verses.24:23: And the brick shall melt away, and the wall shall fall; for the Lord shall reign from Zion and in Jerusalem, and before the elders He shall be glorified.
verses.25:1: O Lord God, I will glorify You, I will sing praise to Your name, for You have done wondrous things, an ancient and true counsel; so be it.
verses.25:2: For You have turned cities into a mound, fortified cities so that their foundations should not fall; the city of the ungodly shall never be built.
verses.25:3: Therefore the poor people shall bless You, and cities of wronged men shall bless You.
verses.25:4: For You have been a helper to every humble city, and a shelter to those who have lost heart because of want; You shall deliver them from wicked men—a shelter for the thirsty, and the spirit of wronged men,
verses.25:5: like fainthearted men thirsting in Zion because of ungodly men, to whom You delivered us.
verses.25:6: And the Lord of hosts shall act for all the nations; upon this mountain they shall drink gladness, they shall drink wine;
verses.25:7: they shall anoint themselves with ointment on this mountain. Deliver all these things to the nations, for this counsel is upon all the nations.
verses.25:8: Death prevailed and swallowed up, and again the Lord God took away every tear from every face; the reproach of the people He took away from all the earth, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.
verses.25:9: And they shall say in that day, "Behold our God, in whom we hoped, and He shall save us; this is the Lord, we waited for Him and exulted, and we shall be glad in our salvation."
verses.25:10: God shall give rest upon this mountain, and the land of Moab shall be trampled down just as they tread a threshing floor with wagons;
verses.25:11: and he shall let down his hands, just as he himself also brought low in order to destroy, and He shall humble his arrogance over the things upon which he laid his hands;
verses.25:12: and the height of the refuge of your wall He shall bring low, and they shall come down to the ground.
verses.26:1: In that day they shall sing this song in the land of Judea: "Behold, a strong city! And He shall appoint salvation as the wall and outer wall.
verses.26:2: Open the gates; let a people keeping righteousness and keeping truth enter,
verses.26:3: laying hold of truth and keeping peace; for in You with hope
verses.26:4: they have hoped, O Lord, forever, the great and eternal God,
verses.26:5: who humbled and brought down those who dwell on high; fortified cities You shall cast down and bring down to the ground,
verses.26:6: and the feet of the meek and lowly shall trample them.
verses.26:7: The way of the godly has become straight; the way of the godly is also prepared.
verses.26:8: For the way of the Lord is judgment; we have hoped in Your name and in the remembrance
verses.26:9: which our soul desires. Out of the night my spirit rises early to You, O God, because Your ordinances are light upon the earth. Learn righteousness, you who dwell upon the earth.
verses.26:10: For the ungodly has ceased; everyone who will not learn righteousness upon the earth shall by no means practice truth; let the ungodly be taken away, lest he see the glory of the Lord.
verses.26:11: O Lord, Your arm is lifted high, and they did not know it; yet when they know, they shall be put to shame; zeal shall seize an untaught people, and now fire shall devour the adversaries.
verses.26:12: O Lord our God, give us peace, for You have rendered all things to us.
verses.26:13: Possess us, O Lord; besides You we do not know another; we name Your name.
verses.26:14: But the dead shall by no means see life, neither shall physicians by any means raise them up; therefore You brought it upon them and destroyed them, and took away every male of theirs.
verses.26:15: Add evils to them, O Lord, add evils to the glorious ones of the earth.
verses.26:16: O Lord, in affliction I remembered You; in a little affliction Your chastening was upon us.
verses.26:17: And as a woman in labor draws near to give birth and cries out in her pangs, so we became to Your beloved.
verses.26:18: Because of the fear of You, O Lord, we conceived and were in labor and gave birth; we have accomplished the spirit of Your salvation upon the earth, yet all who dwell upon the earth shall fall.
verses.26:19: The dead shall rise, and those who are in the tombs shall be raised, and those who are in the earth shall rejoice; for the dew that is from You is healing to them, but the land of the ungodly shall fall."
verses.26:20: Go, My people, enter into your chambers, shut your door, hide yourself for a very little while, until the wrath of the Lord passes by.
verses.26:21: For behold, the Lord from the holy place is bringing wrath upon those who dwell upon the earth; and the earth shall uncover its blood, and shall not cover over those who were slain.
verses.27:1: In that day God shall bring the holy, great, and mighty sword upon the dragon, the fleeing serpent, upon the dragon, the crooked serpent; He shall slay the dragon.
verses.27:2: In that day, a fair vineyard—a desire to begin a song against her.
verses.27:3: I am a strong city, a besieged city; in vain I shall water her, for by night she shall be captured, and by day the wall shall fall.
verses.27:4: There is none that has not laid hold of her. Who will set Me to guard stubble in a field? Because of this hostility I have rejected her. Therefore, because of this, the Lord has done all that He appointed. "I have been burned up,"
verses.27:5: those who dwell in her shall cry out, "Let us make peace."
verses.27:6: Those who are coming, the children of Jacob—Israel shall sprout and blossom, and the inhabited world shall be filled with his fruit.
verses.27:7: As he himself struck, shall he also be struck in the same way? And as he slew, shall he thus be slain?
verses.27:8: Contending and reproaching, He shall send them away; were You not meditating with the harsh spirit, to slay them with a spirit of wrath?
verses.27:9: Therefore the iniquity of Jacob shall be taken away, and this is his blessing, when I take away his sin: when they make all the stones of the altars crushed in pieces like fine dust; and their trees shall by no means remain, and their idols shall be cut down like a forest far away.
verses.27:10: The settled flock shall be abandoned, like a forsaken flock; and for a long time it shall be for a pasture, and there they shall rest.
verses.27:11: And after a time there shall not be any green thing in her, because it has dried up. You women coming from a spectacle, come! For it is not a people having understanding; therefore He who made them shall by no means have compassion, nor shall He who formed them show mercy.
verses.27:12: And it shall come to pass in that day that God shall hedge in from the channel of the river as far as Rhinocorura; and you, gather the sons of Israel one by one.
