verses.49:26: and those who afflicted you shall eat their own flesh, and they shall drink their own blood like new wine and become drunk; and all flesh shall perceive that I am the Lord who redeems you and upholds the strength of Jacob."
verses.50:1: Thus says the Lord: "What is the certificate of divorce of your mother, with which I sent her away? Or to which creditor have I sold you? Behold, for your sins you were sold, and for your iniquities I sent your mother away.
verses.50:2: Why is it that I came, and there was no man? I called, and there was no one who answered? Is My hand not strong enough to redeem? Or do I not have strength to deliver? Behold, by My rebuke I will lay waste the sea, and make rivers desolate; and their fish shall be dried up because there is no water, and they shall die in thirst.
verses.50:3: I will clothe the heaven with darkness, and I will make its covering like sackcloth."
verses.50:4: The Lord gives me a tongue of instruction, to know when it is necessary to speak a word; He appointed it for me in the morning; He added to me an ear to hear,
verses.50:5: and the instruction of the Sovereign Lord opens my ears, and I do not disobey, nor do I speak against it.
verses.50:6: I gave my back to scourges, and my cheeks to blows; and my face I did not turn away from the shame of spitting,
verses.50:7: and the Sovereign Lord became my helper; therefore I was not confounded, but I set my face like a solid rock, and I knew that I shall by no means be put to shame.
verses.50:8: For He who has justified me draws near; who is he who contends with me? Let him stand against me together; and who is he who contends with me? Let him draw near to me.
verses.50:9: Behold, the Lord will help me; who will harm me? Behold, all of you shall grow old like a garment, and a moth shall devour you.
verses.50:10: Who among you fears the Lord? Let him obey the voice of His servant; you who walk in darkness and have no light, trust in the name of the Lord and lean upon God.
verses.50:11: Behold, all of you kindle a fire and strengthen a flame; walk in the light of your fire and in the flame which you have kindled. Because of Me these things have come upon you; you shall lie down in sorrow.
verses.51:1: Listen to Me, you who pursue righteousness and who seek the Lord: look to the solid rock which you hewed out, and to the pit of the cistern which you dug.
verses.51:2: Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who travailed in birth with you; for he was one, and I called him, and blessed him, and loved him.
verses.51:3: And now I will comfort you, Zion, and I have comforted all her desolate places; and I will make her desolate places like a paradise, and the regions toward the west like the paradise of the Lord; gladness and exultation they shall find in her, thanksgiving and the voice of praise.
verses.51:4: Hear Me, hear Me, My people, and you kings, give ear to Me; for a law shall go forth from Me, and My judgment for a light of the nations.
verses.51:5: My righteousness draws near swiftly, and My salvation also shall go forth as light, and in My arm the nations shall hope; the islands shall wait for Me, and in My arm they shall hope.
verses.51:6: Lift up your eyes to heaven, and look upon the earth beneath; for heaven was made firm like smoke, and the earth shall grow old like a garment, and its inhabitants shall die just like these things; but My salvation shall be forever, and My righteousness shall never fail.
verses.51:7: Listen to Me, you who know judgment, you people in whose heart is My law: do not fear the reproach of men, and do not be overcome by their contempt.
verses.51:8: For like a garment it shall be devoured by time, and like wool it shall be devoured by a moth; but My righteousness shall be forever, and My salvation to generations of generations.
verses.51:9: Awake, awake, O Jerusalem, and put on the strength of your arm; awake as in the beginning of the day, as a generation of eternity.
verses.51:10: Are you not she who lays waste the sea, the abundance of the water of the abyss? She who made the depths of the sea a way of passage for the delivered
verses.51:11: and the redeemed? For by the Lord they shall be brought back, and they shall come to Zion with gladness and everlasting exultation; for praise is upon their head, and gladness shall overtake them; pain and grief and sighing have fled away.
verses.51:12: I, even I, am He who comforts you; know who you are, that you were afraid of a mortal man and of a son of man, who have withered like grass.
verses.51:13: And you forgot God who made you, who made heaven and laid the foundation of the earth; and you feared continually, all the days, the face of the wrath of him who afflicts you, because of the manner in which he purposed to take you away. And now, where is the wrath of him who afflicts you?
verses.51:14: For when you are saved, he shall neither stand nor tarry;
verses.51:15: for I am your God, who stirs up the sea and makes its waves roar; the Lord of Sabaoth is My name.
verses.51:16: I will put My words into your mouth, and beneath the shadow of My hand I will shelter you, with which I established heaven and laid the foundation of the earth; and He shall say to Zion, "You are My people."
verses.51:17: Awake, awake, arise, O Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of the Lord the cup of His wrath; for the cup of downfall, the chalice of wrath, you have drunk dry and emptied out,
verses.51:18: and there was no one to comfort you from among all your children whom you bore, and there was no one to take hold of your hand, not even from among all your sons whom you raised up.
verses.51:19: These two things are set against you—who will grieve with you? Downfall and destruction, famine and sword—who will comfort you?
verses.51:20: Your sons are the ones in distress, who sleep at the head of every exit like a half-boiled beet, who are full of the wrath of the Lord, grown faint through the Lord God.
verses.51:21: Therefore hear, you who are humbled and drunk, yet not with wine.
verses.51:22: Thus says the Lord God, who judges His people: "Behold, I have taken out of your hand the cup of downfall, the chalice of My wrath, and you shall no longer drink it again;
verses.51:23: and I will put it into the hands of those who wronged you, those who humbled you, who said to your soul, 'Bow down, that we may pass over'; and you laid your inward parts level with the ground outside for those who passed by."
verses.52:1: Awake, awake, O Zion; put on your strength, O Zion, and put on your glory, O Jerusalem, the holy city; the uncircumcised and the unclean shall no longer pass through you.
verses.52:2: Shake off the dust and arise; take your seat, O Jerusalem; loose the bond from your neck, O captive daughter of Zion.
verses.52:3: For thus says the Lord: "You were sold for nothing, and you shall be redeemed without silver."
verses.52:4: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: "My people went down at the first into Egypt to sojourn there, and to the Assyrians they were led away by force;
verses.52:5: and now, why are you here?" Thus says the Lord: "Because My people were taken away for nothing, marvel and wail." Thus says the Lord: "Because of you, My name is continually blasphemed among the nations.
verses.52:6: Therefore My people shall know My name in that day, that I Myself am He who speaks; I am present, like a season upon the mountains,
verses.52:7: like the feet of him who brings glad tidings of a report of peace, like one bringing glad tidings of good things; for I will make your salvation heard, saying to Zion, 'Your God shall reign.'"
verses.52:8: For the voice of those who guard you has been lifted up, and with the voice together they shall rejoice; for eyes shall look to eyes when the Lord has mercy on Zion.
verses.52:9: Let the desolate places of Jerusalem break forth together into gladness, for the Lord has had mercy on her and has delivered Jerusalem.
verses.52:10: And the Lord shall reveal His holy arm before all the nations, and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation that comes from our God.
verses.52:11: Depart, depart, go out from there, and do not touch what is unclean; go out from her midst, be separated, you who bear the vessels of the Lord;
verses.52:12: for you shall not go out with tumult, nor shall you go by flight; for the Lord shall go forward before you, and the God of Israel who gathers you together.
verses.52:13: Behold, My Servant shall understand, and He shall be exalted and glorified exceedingly.
verses.52:14: Just as many shall be astonished at You, so shall Your appearance be without glory from men, and Your glory from mankind.
verses.52:15: So shall many nations marvel at Him, and kings shall keep their mouth shut; for those to whom it was not declared concerning Him shall see, and those who have not heard shall understand.
verses.53:1: Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?
verses.53:2: We made announcement before Him as a little child, as a root in a thirsty land; He has no form nor glory. And we beheld Him, and He had no form nor beauty;
verses.53:3: rather, His form was without honor, failing beyond the sons of men—a man in affliction and knowing how to bear infirmity, for His countenance is turned away; He was dishonored and was not esteemed.
verses.53:4: This One bears our sins and suffers anguish on our behalf; yet we esteemed Him to be in travail, and in affliction, and in ill-treatment.
verses.53:5: But He was wounded because of our sins, and He has been made weak because of our iniquities; the chastisement of our peace was upon Him, and by His bruise we were healed.
verses.53:6: All of us like sheep went astray; each man wandered in his own way; and the Lord delivered Him up to our sins.
verses.53:7: And He, because He has been afflicted, does not open His mouth; as a sheep He was led to slaughter, and as a lamb before its shearer is silent, so He does not open His mouth.
verses.53:8: In His humiliation His judgment was taken away; who shall declare His generation? For His life is taken away from the earth; because of the iniquities of My people He was led to death.
verses.53:9: And I will give the wicked in place of His burial, and the rich in place of His death; because He wrought no iniquity, nor was deceit found in His mouth.
verses.53:10: And the Lord wills to cleanse Him from the affliction; if you give an offering for sin, our soul shall behold a long-lived seed.
verses.53:11: And the Lord wills to take away from the travail of His soul, to show Him light and to form Him with understanding, to justify a righteous One who serves many well; and their sins He Himself shall bear.
verses.53:12: Therefore He shall inherit many, and He shall divide the spoils of the strong, because His soul was delivered up to death, and He was reckoned among the lawless; and He Himself bore the sins of many, and because of their iniquities He was delivered up.
verses.54:1: Be glad, O barren one who does not bear; break forth and cry aloud, you who do not travail in birth; for many more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has the husband, for the Lord has spoken.
verses.54:2: Enlarge the place of your tent and of your curtains; pitch it, do not spare; lengthen your cords, and strengthen your stakes,
verses.54:3: stretch out yet further to the right and to the left; and your seed shall inherit nations, and you shall settle desolate cities.
verses.54:4: Do not fear because you were put to shame, nor be abashed because you were reproached; for you shall forget everlasting shame, and the reproach of your widowhood you shall remember no more.
verses.54:5: For the Lord is He who makes you, the Lord of Sabaoth is His name; and He who delivered you shall Himself be called the God of Israel for all the earth.
verses.54:6: The Lord has not called you as a forsaken and fainthearted woman, nor as a woman hated from youth, said your God.
verses.54:7: For a brief time I forsook you, and with great mercy I will have mercy on you;
verses.54:8: in a little wrath I turned My face away from you, and with everlasting mercy I will have mercy on you, said the Lord who delivered you.
verses.54:9: From the water that was in the time of Noah, this is to Me: just as I swore to him in that time to the earth, that I would no longer be angry with you, nor in a threat against you should the mountains be removed,
verses.54:10: nor shall your hills be shaken; so neither shall the mercy from Me to you fail, nor shall the covenant of your peace ever be removed; for He said, "Gracious to you, O Lord."
verses.54:11: Humbled and unsettled, you were not comforted; behold, I am preparing carbuncle for your stone, and sapphire for your foundations,
verses.54:12: and I will make your battlements jasper, and your gates stones of crystal, and your surrounding wall choice stones,
verses.54:13: and all your sons taught of God, and your children in great peace.
verses.54:14: And in righteousness you shall be built up; keep away from injustice, and you shall not fear, and trembling shall not draw near to you.
verses.54:15: Behold, proselytes shall come to you through Me, and they shall sojourn with you and shall flee to you for refuge.
verses.54:16: Behold, I have created you, not as a coppersmith blowing upon coals and bringing forth an instrument for work; but I created you not to ruin for destruction.
verses.54:17: Every instrument fashioned against you I will not cause to prosper; and every voice that shall rise against you in judgment, all of them you shall defeat, and those who are guilty against you shall be in it. There is an inheritance for those who serve the Lord, and you shall be righteous to Me, says the Lord.
verses.55:1: You who thirst, go to the water, and all you who have no silver, go forth and buy, and eat, without silver and price, wine and fat.
verses.55:2: Why do you pay a price in silver, and your labor not for satisfaction? And you shall eat good things, and your soul shall delight itself in good things.
verses.55:3: Give heed with your ears and follow after My ways; listen to Me, and your soul shall live in good things; and I will make with you an everlasting covenant, the faithful holy things of David.
verses.55:4: Behold, I have given him as a testimony among the nations, a ruler and commander to the nations.
verses.55:5: Nations that do not know you shall call upon you, and peoples who are not acquainted with you shall flee for refuge to you, for the sake of the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, because He has glorified you.
verses.55:6: Seek the Lord, and upon finding Him, call upon Him; and whenever He draws near to you,
verses.55:7: let the ungodly forsake his ways and a lawless man his counsels, and let him return to the Lord, and he shall receive mercy; for He will abundantly forgive your sins.
verses.55:8: "For My counsels are not like your counsels, nor are My ways like your ways," says the Lord;
verses.55:9: "but as heaven is distant from the earth, so is My way distant from your ways, and your thoughts from My mind.
verses.55:10: For just as rain or snow descends from heaven and shall by no means return until it drenches the earth, and makes it bring forth and sprout, and gives seed to the sower and bread for food,
verses.55:11: so shall My word be that goes forth from My mouth; it shall by no means return until all things that I have willed are accomplished, and I will prosper your ways and My commandments."
verses.55:12: For in gladness you shall go forth, and in joy you shall be taught; for the mountains and the hills shall leap up, welcoming you in joy, and all the trees of the field shall clap with their branches,
verses.55:13: and instead of the thornbush shall come up the cypress, and instead of the fleabane shall come up the myrtle; and the Lord shall be for a name and for an everlasting sign, and it shall not fail.
verses.56:1: Thus says the Lord: "Keep justice and do righteousness, for My salvation has drawn near to come, and My mercy to be revealed."
verses.56:2: Blessed is the man who does these things, and the mortal who holds fast to them, who keeps the Sabbaths so as not to profane them, and who guards his hands from doing unjust deeds.
verses.56:3: Do not let the foreigner who has joined himself to the Lord say, "Surely the Lord will separate me from His people"; and do not let the eunuch say, "I am a dry tree."
verses.56:4: Thus says the Lord to the eunuchs: "As many as keep My Sabbaths, and choose the things that I desire, and hold fast to My covenant,
verses.56:5: I will give to them in My house and within My wall a place of renown, better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, and it shall not fail.
verses.56:6: And as for the foreigners who have joined themselves to the Lord to serve Him, and to love the name of the Lord, so as to be His male servants and female servants, and all who keep My Sabbaths so as not to profane them and who hold fast to My covenant—
verses.56:7: I will bring them into My holy mountain and make them glad in My house of prayer; their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be acceptable upon My altar. For My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations,"
verses.56:8: said the Lord who gathers the dispersed of Israel, "for I will gather a congregation to him."
verses.56:9: All you wild beasts, come and eat, all you beasts of the forest.
verses.56:10: See that they have all been blinded; they have not understood; mute dogs, they shall not be able to bark, dreaming of a bed, loving to slumber.
verses.56:11: And the dogs are shameless in soul, not knowing satisfaction; and they are wicked, not knowing understanding; they have all followed their own ways, each one according to his own.
verses.57:1: See how the righteous man has perished, and no one takes it to heart; and righteous men are taken away, and no one considers it. For from before unrighteousness the righteous man has been taken away;
verses.57:2: his burial shall be in peace; he has been taken away from the midst.
verses.57:3: But as for you, draw near here, you lawless sons, offspring of adulterers and a harlot:
verses.57:4: At whom have you made sport? And against whom have you opened your mouth? And against whom have you let loose your tongue? Are you not children of destruction, a lawless offspring—
verses.57:5: those who invoke the idols under thick trees, slaughtering their children in the valleys in the midst of the rocks?
verses.57:6: That is your portion, this is your lot; and to those you poured out drink offerings, and to these you offered up sacrifices. At these things, therefore, shall I not be angry?
verses.57:7: Upon a high and lofty mountain, there is your bed, and there you brought up sacrifices;
verses.57:8: and behind the posts of your door you placed your memorials. You supposed that if you departed from Me, you would have something more; you loved those who slept with you,
verses.57:9: and you multiplied your harlotry with them, and you increased those who are far from you; and you sent envoys beyond your borders, and you were brought low even to Hades.
verses.57:10: In your many journeys you grew weary, and you did not say, "I will cease," growing strong because you did these things; therefore you did not implore Me.
verses.57:11: Whom did you dread and fear, that you lied to Me and did not remember, nor took Me into your mind nor into your heart? And seeing you, I overlook you, and Me you did not fear.
verses.57:12: And I will declare your righteousness and your evil deeds, which shall not profit you.
verses.57:13: When you cry aloud, let them deliver you in your affliction; for the wind shall take all of these, and a tempest shall carry them away. But those who hold fast to Me shall possess the land and shall inherit My holy mountain,
verses.57:14: and they shall say, "Clear the ways before him, and remove stumbling blocks from the way of My people."
verses.57:15: Thus says the Most High in the highest places, who inhabits eternity, Holy among the holy ones is His name, the Most High who rests among the holy ones, and gives longsuffering to the fainthearted, and gives life to those who are contrite in heart:
verses.57:16: "I will not take vengeance on you forever, nor will I be angry with you continually; for a spirit shall go forth from Me, and every breath I have made.
verses.57:17: Because of sin for a little while I grieved him, and I struck him and turned My face away from him; and he was grieved, and went downcast in his ways.
verses.57:18: I have seen his ways, and I healed him and comforted him, and I gave him true consolation,
verses.57:19: peace upon peace to those who are far off and to those who are near." And the Lord said, "I will heal them."
verses.57:20: But the unrighteous shall be tossed like waves and shall not be able to rest.
verses.57:21: "There is no rejoicing," said God, "for the ungodly."
verses.58:1: Cry aloud with strength and do not spare; lift up your voice like a trumpet, and declare to My people their sins, and to the house of Jacob their iniquities.
verses.58:2: Day after day they seek Me, and they desire to know My ways, as a people who have practiced righteousness and have not forsaken the judgment of their God; now they ask of Me righteous judgment, and they desire to draw near to God,
verses.58:3: saying, "Why is it that we have fasted, and You did not see? We have humbled our souls, and You did not know?" For in the days of your fasts you find your own desires, and you goad all those who are under your hand.
verses.58:4: If you fast for disputes and quarrels, and strike a lowly man with fists, why do you fast for Me as today, so that your voice may be heard in outcry?
verses.58:5: This is not the fast that I have chosen, nor a day for a man to humble his soul; not even if you bend your neck like a ring, and spread sackcloth and ashes beneath yourself, not even so shall you call it an acceptable fast.
verses.58:6: I have not chosen such a fast, says the Lord; rather, loose every bond of injustice, untie the knots of oppressive contracts, send forth the broken in liberty, and tear apart every unjust written bond.
verses.58:7: Break your bread for the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; if you see a naked man, clothe him, and you shall not disregard the kinsmen of your own seed.
verses.58:8: Then your light shall break forth early, and your healings shall swiftly spring up; your righteousness shall go before you, and the glory of God shall envelop you.
verses.58:9: Then you shall cry out, and God will listen to you; while you are still speaking, He will say, "Behold, I am here." If you remove from yourself a bond, the stretching out of the hand, and a word of murmuring,
verses.58:10: and give bread from your soul to the hungry, and satisfy a humbled soul, then your light shall rise in the darkness, and your darkness shall be as noonday.
verses.58:11: And your God shall be with you continually; you shall be filled just as your soul desires, and your bones shall be fattened, and they shall be like a well-watered garden and like a spring which water has not failed.
verses.58:12: And your ancient wastes shall be built up, and your foundations shall be everlasting for generations of generations; you shall be called Builder of Fences, and you shall bring your pathways in the midst to rest.
verses.58:13: If you turn back your foot from the Sabbaths, so as not to do your own desires on the holy day, and call the Sabbaths delightful, holy to God, and do not lift your foot for work, nor speak a word in anger from your mouth,
verses.58:14: then you shall trust in the Lord, and He shall bring you up upon the good things of the earth, and feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things.
verses.59:1: Is the hand of the Lord not strong enough to save? Or has His ear grown heavy, so that He cannot listen?
verses.59:2: Rather, your sins separate between you and God, and because of your sins He has turned His face away from you, so as not to show mercy.
verses.59:3: For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with sins; your lips have spoken iniquity, and your tongue meditates on injustice.
verses.59:4: No one speaks what is righteous, nor is there true judgment; they trust in vain things and speak empty words, for they conceive trouble and bring forth iniquity.
verses.59:5: They have broken open the eggs of asps and weave a spider's web; he who is about to eat of their eggs, upon crushing one, finds a rotten egg, and within it is a basilisk.
verses.59:6: Their web shall not serve as a garment, nor shall they clothe themselves with their works; for their works are works of iniquity.
verses.59:7: Their feet run to wickedness, swift to shed blood, and their thoughts come from murders; ruin and misery are in their ways,
verses.59:8: and the way of peace they do not know, and there is no justice in their ways; for the paths which they travel are crooked, and they do not know peace.
verses.59:9: Therefore justice has departed from them, and righteousness shall by no means overtake them; while they waited for light, darkness came upon them; waiting for brightness, they walked in the dead of night.
verses.59:10: They shall grope for a wall like the blind, and as those who have no eyes they shall grope; they shall fall at noonday as at midnight; like dying men they shall groan;
verses.59:11: like a bear and like a dove they shall go together. We waited for justice, and there is none; salvation has withdrawn far from us.
verses.59:12: For our iniquity is great before You, and our sins have stood against us; for our iniquities are within us, and we have known our wrongdoings:
verses.59:13: we have acted impiously and lied, and turned away from following our God; we have spoken unjust things and have been disobedient; we conceived and meditated from our heart unjust words,
verses.59:14: and we have thrust justice back, and righteousness has stood far off; for truth has been consumed in their ways, and they could not pass through by a straight way.
verses.59:15: And truth has been taken away, and they turned their mind away from understanding. And the Lord saw it, and it did not please Him, because there was no justice.
verses.59:16: And He looked, and there was no man, and He observed, and there was no one to help; and He defended them with His arm, and with mercy He upheld Himself.
verses.59:17: And He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and placed a helmet of salvation upon His head; and He clothed Himself with a garment of vengeance and with His mantle,
verses.59:18: as One about to render recompense—reproach to the adversaries.
verses.59:19: And those from the west shall fear the name of the Lord, and those from the rising of the sun the glorious name; for the wrath from the Lord shall come like a violent river; it shall come with fury.
verses.59:20: And the Deliverer shall come for the sake of Zion, and He shall turn away impieties from Jacob.
verses.59:21: "And this is the covenant from Me for them," says the Lord: "My Spirit who is upon you, and the words which I have put into your mouth, shall by no means fail from your mouth and from the mouth of your seed"—for the Lord has spoken—"from this time forth and forever."
verses.60:1: Shine, shine, O Jerusalem, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.
verses.60:2: Behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and gloom upon the nations; but the Lord shall appear upon you, and His glory shall be seen upon you.
verses.60:3: And kings shall walk in your light, and nations in your brightness.
verses.60:4: Lift up your eyes all around and see your children gathered together; all your sons have come from afar, and your daughters shall be carried upon shoulders.
verses.60:5: Then you shall see, and you shall fear and be amazed in heart, because the wealth of the sea and of nations and of peoples shall turn over to you. And herds of camels shall come to you,
verses.60:6: and the camels of Midian and Ephah shall cover you; all from Sheba shall come bringing gold, and they shall bring frankincense, and they shall proclaim the glad tidings of the salvation of the Lord.
verses.60:7: And all the sheep of Kedar shall be gathered together, and the rams of Nebaioth shall come; acceptable offerings shall be brought up upon My altar, and the house of My prayer shall be glorified.
verses.60:8: Who are these who fly like clouds, and like doves with nestlings to Me?
verses.60:9: For Me the islands have waited, and the ships of Tarshish among the first, to bring your children from afar, and their silver and their gold with them, and the holy name of the Lord, and because the Holy One of Israel is glorious.
verses.60:10: And foreigners shall build your walls, and their kings shall attend upon you; for because of My wrath I struck you, and because of mercy I have loved you.
verses.60:11: And your gates shall be opened continually; day and night they shall not be shut, to bring into you the might of nations and their kings led in.
verses.60:12: For the nations and the kings who will not serve you shall perish, and the nations shall be made desolate with desolation.
verses.60:13: And the glory of Lebanon shall come to you with cypress and pine and cedar together, to glorify My holy place.
verses.60:14: And the sons of those who humbled you and provoked you shall come to you in fear, and you shall be called City of the Lord, Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
verses.60:15: Because you have been forsaken and hated, and there was no one to help, I will make you an everlasting rejoicing, a gladness for generations of generations.
verses.60:16: And you shall nurse on the milk of nations, and you shall eat the wealth of kings; and you shall know that I am the Lord who saves you, and the God of Israel who delivers you.
verses.60:17: Instead of bronze I will bring you gold, and instead of iron I will bring you silver, and instead of wood I will bring you bronze, and instead of stones, iron. And I will appoint your rulers in peace, and your overseers in righteousness.
verses.60:18: And injustice shall no longer be heard in your land, neither ruin nor misery within your borders; rather, your walls shall be called Salvation, and your gates, Engraving.
verses.60:19: And the sun shall no longer be for you the light of day, nor shall the rising of the moon illuminate the night for you; rather, the Lord shall be for you an everlasting light, and God your glory.
verses.60:20: For the sun shall not set for you, and the moon shall not fail you; for the Lord shall be for you an everlasting light, and the days of your mourning shall be fulfilled.
verses.60:21: And your people shall all be righteous; forever they shall inherit the land, guarding the planting, the works of His hands for glory.
verses.60:22: The smallest one shall become thousands, and the least one a great nation; I, the Lord, will gather them in due season.
verses.61:1: The Spirit of the Lord is upon Me, because He has anointed Me; He has sent Me to declare glad tidings to the poor, to heal those who are broken in heart, to herald release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind,
verses.61:2: to declare an acceptable year of the Lord and a day of recompense, to console all those who mourn,
verses.61:3: that to them, those who mourn in Zion, glory may be given in place of ashes, the ointment of gladness to the mourners, a mantle of glory instead of a spirit of despondency; and they shall be called generations of righteousness, a planting of the Lord for glory.
verses.61:4: And they shall build up ancient wastelands; those formerly laid desolate they shall raise up; and they shall renew deserted cities, laid waste for generations.
verses.61:5: And foreigners shall come tending your sheep, and men of other nations as plowmen and vinedressers;
verses.61:6: but you shall be called priests of the Lord, ministers of God; the strength of the nations you shall consume, and in their wealth you shall be marveled at.
verses.61:7: Thus they shall inherit the land a second time, and everlasting gladness shall be upon their head.
verses.61:8: For I am the Lord, who loves righteousness and hates plunder from unrighteousness; and I will give their labor to the righteous, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with them.
verses.61:9: And their seed shall be known among the nations, and their offspring in the midst of the peoples; everyone who sees them shall recognize them, that these are a seed blessed by God,
verses.61:10: and with gladness they shall rejoice in the Lord. Let my soul exult in the Lord, for He has clothed me with a garment of salvation and a tunic of gladness; He has placed a turban upon me like a bridegroom, and like a bride He has adorned me with ornament.
verses.61:11: And as the earth causes its blossom to grow, and as a garden its seeds, so the Lord, the Lord will cause righteousness and exultation to spring forth before all the nations.
verses.62:1: For the sake of Zion I will not keep silent, and for the sake of Jerusalem I will not relent, until her righteousness goes forth like light, and My salvation shall burn like a torch.
verses.62:2: And nations shall see your righteousness, and kings your glory; and He shall call you by the new name that the Lord shall name.
verses.62:3: And you shall be a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord, and a diadem of a kingdom in the hand of your God.
verses.62:4: And no longer shall you be called "Forsaken," and your land shall no longer be called "Desolate"; for you shall be called "My Good Pleasure," and your land "Inhabited," because the Lord has delighted in you, and your land shall be inhabited.
verses.62:5: And as a young man dwells with a virgin, so shall your sons dwell; and it shall come to pass that just as a bridegroom rejoices over a bride, so shall the Lord rejoice over you.
verses.62:6: And upon your walls, O Jerusalem, I have appointed watchmen all the day and all the night, who continually shall not keep silent, remembering the Lord.
verses.62:7: For there is none like you, if He sets aright and makes Jerusalem a boast upon the earth.
verses.62:8: The Lord has sworn by His glory and by the strength of His arm: "Surely I will no longer give your grain and food to your enemies, and surely foreign sons shall no longer drink your wine for which you have labored;
verses.62:9: but those who gather them shall eat them and praise the Lord, and those who gather them shall drink them in My holy courts."
verses.62:10: Go through My gates, and make a way for My people, and cast the stones from the way; lift up a banner to the nations.
verses.62:11: For behold, the Lord has made it heard to the end of the earth; say to the daughter of Zion, "Behold, the Savior has come to you, having His own reward, and His work before His face."
verses.62:12: And He shall call them "A Holy People, Redeemed by the Lord," and you shall be called "A Sought-Out City" and "Not Forsaken."
verses.63:1: Who is this who comes from Edom, with redness of garments from Bozrah, so stately in apparel, with force and strength? "I declare righteousness and judgment of salvation."
verses.63:2: Why are Your garments red, and Your raiment like that from a trodden winepress?
verses.63:3: "I am full of the trodden winepress, and of the nations there is not a man with Me; and I trampled them in My fury, and crushed them like earth, and brought down their blood.
verses.63:4: For a day of recompense has come upon them, and a year of redemption is at hand.
verses.63:5: And I looked, and there was no helper; and I considered, and no one lent support; so My arm delivered them, and My fury stood ready.
verses.63:6: And I trampled them in My wrath, and brought down their blood to the earth."
verses.63:7: I called to mind the mercy of the Lord, the excellencies of the Lord in all that He recompenses to us. The Lord is a good judge to the house of Israel; He brings upon us according to His mercy and according to the multitude of His righteousness.
verses.63:8: And He said, "Are they not My people? Children, they will surely not deal falsely." And He became salvation to them
verses.63:9: out of all their affliction. Neither an envoy nor an angel, but He Himself saved them, because He loved them and spared them; He Himself redeemed them and took them up, and exalted them all the days of old;
verses.63:10: but they disobeyed and provoked His Holy Spirit; so He was turned to enmity against them, and He Himself warred against them.
verses.63:11: And he remembered the days of old: "Where is He who brought up from the sea the shepherd of the sheep? Where is He who placed the Holy Spirit within them,
verses.63:12: who led Moses by the right hand, the arm of His glory?" He prevailed over the water before him, to make for Himself an everlasting name.
verses.63:13: He led them through the deep like a horse through a wilderness, and they did not grow weary,
verses.63:14: and like cattle through a plain; the Spirit came down from the Lord and guided them; thus You led Your people, to make for Yourself a name of glory.
verses.63:15: Turn from heaven and look from Your holy house and Your glory; where is Your zeal and Your strength? Where is the multitude of Your mercy and Your compassions, that You have held back from us?
verses.63:16: For You are our Father, because Abraham did not know us, and Israel did not acknowledge us; but You, O Lord, are our Father; deliver us; from the beginning Your name is upon us.
verses.63:17: Why have You caused us to stray, O Lord, from Your way? Have You hardened our hearts so as not to fear You? Return for the sake of Your servants, for the sake of the tribes of Your inheritance,
verses.63:18: that for a little while we may inherit Your holy mountain.
verses.63:19: We have become as at the beginning, when You did not rule over us, nor was Your name called upon us. If You open heaven, trembling shall seize the mountains from You, and they shall melt
verses.64:1: As wax melts before fire, fire shall also burn up the adversaries, and Your name shall be manifest among the adversaries; at Your presence nations shall be troubled,
verses.64:2: when You perform glorious deeds; trembling shall seize the mountains before You.
verses.64:3: From of old we have not heard, nor have our eyes seen a God besides You, and Your works which You will do for those who wait for mercy.
verses.64:4: It shall meet those who do what is right, and they shall remember Your ways. Behold, You were angry, and we sinned; therefore we went astray,
verses.64:5: and we have all become as those who are unclean, and all our righteousness is like the rag of a woman in her impurity; we have fallen away like leaves because of our iniquities, and thus the wind shall carry us away.
verses.64:6: And there is no one who calls upon Your name, nor who remembers to take hold of You; for You have turned Your face away from us, and have delivered us up because of our sins.
verses.64:7: And now, O Lord, You are our Father; we are clay, and all of us are the works of Your hands.
verses.64:8: Do not be exceedingly angry with us, and do not remember our sins in due time; and now look upon us, for all of us are Your people.
verses.64:9: The city of Your sanctuary, Zion, has become a wilderness; Jerusalem has become like a wilderness—for a curse.
verses.64:10: The house, our sanctuary, and the glory which our fathers blessed have been burned with fire, and all our glorious things have fallen into ruin.
verses.64:11: And for all these things You have restrained Yourself, O Lord, and have kept silent, and have humbled us exceedingly.
verses.65:1: I became manifest to those who did not inquire of Me; I was found by those who did not seek Me. I said, "Here I am," to a nation that did not call upon My name.
verses.65:2: I stretched out My hands all the day to a disobedient and contrary people, to those who walk in a way that is not good, but after their sins.
verses.65:3: This is the people that provokes Me continually before My face; they offer sacrifices in the gardens and burn incense upon the bricks to demons that do not exist,
verses.65:4: who lie down to sleep in the tombs and in the caves for the sake of dreams, who eat swine's flesh and the broth of sacrifices—all their vessels are defiled—
verses.65:5: who say, "Stay far from me, do not come near me, for I am pure." This is the smoke of My wrath; a fire burns in it all the days.
verses.65:6: Behold, it is written before Me: "I will not keep silent until I repay into their bosom
verses.65:7: their sins and the sins of their fathers," says the Lord, "who burned incense upon the mountains and reproached Me upon the hills; I will repay their works into their bosom."
verses.65:8: Thus says the Lord: "Just as the grape shall be found in the cluster, and they shall say, 'Do not destroy it, for a blessing is in it,' so will I do for the sake of him who serves Me; for his sake I will by no means destroy them all.
verses.65:9: And I will bring forth the seed out of Jacob and out of Judah, and it shall inherit My holy mountain; and My chosen ones and My servants shall inherit it, and they shall dwell there.
verses.65:10: And there shall be folds for flocks in the forest, and the Valley of Achor shall be a resting place for herds, for My people who have sought Me.
verses.65:11: But as for you who forsake Me and forget My holy mountain, who prepare a table for the demon and fill a mixed drink for Fortune,
verses.65:12: I will deliver you up to the sword, and all of you shall fall in slaughter; because I called you and you did not obey, I spoke and you refused to heed, and you did evil before Me and chose the things that I did not desire."
verses.65:13: Therefore thus says the Lord: "Behold, those who serve Me shall eat, but you shall hunger; behold, those who serve Me shall drink, but you shall thirst; behold, those who serve Me shall be glad, but you shall be put to shame;
verses.65:14: behold, those who serve Me shall exult in gladness, but you shall cry out for anguish of heart, and from the crushing of your spirit you shall wail.
verses.65:15: For you shall leave your name for a satiety to My chosen ones, and the Lord shall slay you; but upon those who serve Me a new name shall be called,
verses.65:16: which shall be blessed upon the earth; for they shall bless the true God, and those who swear upon the earth shall swear by the true God. For they shall forget the former affliction, and it shall not come up into their heart.
verses.65:17: For the heaven shall be new and the earth shall be new, and they shall by no means remember the former things, nor shall they ever come upon their heart;
verses.65:18: rather, they shall find gladness and exultation in it; for behold, I make Jerusalem an exultation and My people a gladness.
verses.65:19: And I will exult over Jerusalem and be glad over My people; and no longer shall the voice of weeping or the voice of crying be heard in her,
verses.65:20: nor shall there any longer be there one who dies untimely, nor an aged man who does not fulfill his time; for the youth shall be one hundred years old, and the sinner who dies at one hundred years old shall also be accursed.
verses.65:21: And they shall build houses and themselves dwell in them, and they shall plant vineyards and themselves eat their produce;
verses.65:22: they shall by no means build and others dwell in them, nor shall they plant and others eat. For as the days of the tree of life shall be the days of My people; for they shall wear out the works of their labors.
verses.65:23: My chosen ones shall not toil in vain, nor bear children for a curse, because they are a seed blessed by God, and their offspring are with them.
verses.65:24: And it shall come to pass that before they cry out, I will heed them; while they are still speaking, I will say, 'What is it?'
verses.65:25: Then wolves and lambs shall pasture together, and a lion shall eat straw like an ox, and a serpent shall eat earth as bread; they shall neither harm nor destroy upon My holy mountain," says the Lord.
verses.66:1: Thus says the Lord: "Heaven is My throne, and the earth is the footstool of My feet. What sort of house will you build for Me? And what is the place of My rest?
verses.66:2: For all these things My hand has made, and all these things are Mine," says the Lord; "and upon whom shall I look, except upon him who is humble and quiet, and who trembles at My words?
verses.66:3: But the lawless one who sacrifices a calf to Me is like one who kills a dog, and he who offers fine flour is like one who offers swine's blood, and he who gives frankincense for a memorial is like a blasphemer. And they have chosen their own ways, and their soul has desired their abominations;
verses.66:4: so I also will take up their mockeries, and I will repay their sins to them; because I called them and they did not obey Me, I spoke and they did not listen, and they did evil before Me and chose the things that I did not desire."
verses.66:5: Hear the words of the Lord, you who tremble at His word: Say, O our brethren, to those who hate you and abhor you, that the name of the Lord may be glorified and appear in their gladness, and those others shall be put to shame.
verses.66:6: A voice of outcry from the city, a voice from the temple, the voice of the Lord rendering recompense to the adversaries.
verses.66:7: Before she who was in labor gave birth, before the pain of travail came, she escaped and brought forth a male child.
verses.66:8: Who has heard such a thing, and who has seen it thus? Has a land been in labor in one day, or has a nation also been born all at once? For Zion has travailed and brought forth her children.
verses.66:9: "Yet I gave this expectation, and you did not remember Me," said the Lord. "Behold, did I not make both her who bears and her who is barren?" said your God.
verses.66:10: Be glad, O Jerusalem, and hold a festival in her, all you who love her; rejoice with joy together with her, all of you who mourn over her,
verses.66:11: that you may nurse and be satisfied from the breast of her consolation, that having nursed to the full you may delight yourselves from the entrance of her glory.
verses.66:12: For thus says the Lord: "Behold, I turn aside toward them like a river of peace, and like an overflowing torrent the glory of the nations; their children shall be borne upon shoulders and comforted upon knees.
verses.66:13: As one whom a mother comforts, so I also will comfort you, and in Jerusalem you shall be comforted.
verses.66:14: And you shall see, and your heart shall rejoice, and your bones shall spring up like tender grass; and the hand of the Lord shall be known to those who fear Him, and He shall threaten the disobedient."
verses.66:15: For behold, the Lord will come as fire, and His chariots as a tempest, to render His vengeance in wrath and His utter rejection in a flame of fire.
verses.66:16: For by the fire of the Lord all the earth shall be judged, and by His sword all flesh; many shall be wounded by the Lord.
verses.66:17: "Those who sanctify themselves and purify themselves for the gardens, and who in the doorways eat swine's flesh and the abominations and the mouse, shall be consumed together," said the Lord.
verses.66:18: "And I—their works and their reasoning—I am coming to gather all the nations and the tongues, and they shall come and behold My glory.
verses.66:19: And I will leave a sign upon them, and I will send forth those who are saved from among them to the nations—to Tarshish and Put and Lud and Meshech, and to Tubal and to Greece and the islands far off—who have neither heard My name nor seen My glory; and they shall declare My glory among the nations.
verses.66:20: And they shall bring your brethren out of all the nations as a gift to the Lord, with horses and chariots, in covered mule-wagons with canopies, to the holy city Jerusalem," said the Lord, "just as the sons of Israel would bring their sacrifices to Me with psalms into the house of the Lord.
verses.66:21: And from among them I will take priests and Levites," said the Lord.
verses.66:22: "For just as the new heaven and the new earth which I make remain before Me," says the Lord, "so shall your seed and your name stand.
verses.66:23: And it shall come to pass from month to month and from Sabbath to Sabbath that all flesh shall come to worship before Me in Jerusalem," said the Lord.
verses.66:24: "And they shall go forth and look upon the corpses of the men who have transgressed against Me; for their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched, and they shall be a spectacle to all flesh."

notes.1:1: Greek has "against Judea" (kata tes Ioudaias), using the territorial name Judea rather than Judah and the preposition "against," which contrasts with "concerning" (peri) in 2:1.
notes.1:6: The Greek places negative conjunctions ("neither ... nor ... nor") before the three terms for injuries, creating an abrupt construction emphasizing that no remedy—poultice, oil, or bandages—is available.
notes.1:9: "The Lord of hosts" renders Greek Kyrios sabaoth ("Lord Sabaoth"), and "seed" preserves Greek sperma, the Septuagint wording cited in Romans 9:29.
notes.1:18: The Greek uses the first-person active verb leukano ("I will make white") twice, portraying the Lord Himself actively whitening their sins.
notes.2:6: Greek allophylon ("foreigners") is the standard Septuagint designation for the Philistines, here matching the same root in "foreign children" (tekna allophyla).
notes.2:9: The Greek shifts into the first-person singular (ou me aneso autous, "I will by no means forgive them"), expressing the Lord's own verdict directly.
notes.2:11: The Greek reads "the eyes of the Lord are lofty, while man is lowly," contrasting divine majesty with human lowliness rather than referring to human haughtiness.
notes.2:20: Greek tois mataiois literally means "to the vain things" (corresponding to the Hebrew phrase often translated "to the moles"); in the Septuagint, chapter 2 concludes at verse 21.
notes.3:1: The Greek retains the Hebrew title Sabaoth ("hosts") untranslated as Kyrios Sabaoth, and renders the paired support terms as masculine and feminine participles ("the strong man and the strong woman") echoing "strength of bread and strength of water."
notes.3:6: The Greek reads "my food" (to broma to emon), a distinctive Septuagint reading where the Masoretic Hebrew reads "this heap of ruins."
notes.3:10: The Septuagint reads "Let us bind the righteous one, because he is burdensome to us" (echoed in Wisdom 2:12), differing markedly from the Masoretic Hebrew ("Say to the righteous that it shall be well").
notes.3:22: "Laconian garments" (Lakonika) is a Septuagint-distinct Hellenistic term referring to sheer, finely woven Spartan textiles.
notes.3:26: The Greek reads "the cases of your adornment" (hai thekai tou kosmou hymon), referring to jewel chests rather than the Masoretic Hebrew "her gates."
notes.4:2: The Septuagint reads "God shall shine forth in counsel with glory," differing from the Masoretic Hebrew reference to "the Branch of the Lord."
notes.4:4: The Greek explicitly includes "the sons and the daughters of Zion," whereas the Masoretic Hebrew mentions only the daughters.
notes.4:5: The Greek opens with "And He will come" (kai hexei), where the Masoretic Hebrew reads "and the Lord will create."
notes.5:1: "On a horn" (en kerati) renders literally the idiom for a hillside spur; the Greek also introduces the first-person "my vineyard" here and maintains first-person verbs throughout verses 2–7.
notes.5:2: "Sorek" transliterates the Greek loanword sorek (a choice red vine), and the Septuagint reads "thorns" (akanthas) where the Masoretic Hebrew reads "wild grapes."
notes.5:10: "Six artabas" and "three measures" preserve the Septuagint's Hellenistic Egyptian dry-measure terminology and quantities rather than the Hebrew homer and ephah.
notes.5:17: The Septuagint reads "those who were plundered shall graze like bulls," a distinctive Greek rendering differing from the Masoretic Hebrew image of lambs grazing in pasture.
notes.6:1: The Greek reads "the house was full of His glory," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's description of the hem of His robe filling the temple.
notes.6:3: "Sabaoth" preserves the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew divine title meaning "of hosts" or "of armies."
notes.6:10: Rather than the Hebrew imperatives ("Make the heart of this people dull"), the Greek uses past indicatives stating that the people themselves have grown thick of heart and shut their eyes (a reading quoted in Matthew 13:15 and Acts 28:27).
notes.6:12: The Greek reads "those who are left shall be multiplied upon the land" (diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's reference to many forsaken places), and 6:13 likewise concludes with the acorn falling from its husk without the Hebrew's final phrase about a "holy seed."
notes.7:3: The Greek translates the first element of the Hebrew name Shear-Jashub ("a remnant," rendered "who is left") while transliterating the second element ("Jashub").
notes.7:4: The closing promise ("for when the wrath of My anger comes, I shall heal again") is a distinctive Greek reading contrasting with the Hebrew Masoretic Text's mention of the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram.
notes.7:9: The Greek "neither shall you understand" differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's wordplay "you shall not be established."
notes.7:14: The Greek specifies "the virgin" (Greek parthenos, quoted in Matthew 1:23) and uses the second-person singular verb "you shall call."
notes.7:18: The Greek reads "which shall rule over part of the river of Egypt," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to the fly at the farthest streams of Egypt.
notes.8:1: Here and in 8:3 the Greek translates the symbolic Hebrew name Maher-Shalal-Hash-Baz ("Quickly Spoil, Swiftly Plunder") rather than transliterating it.
notes.8:8: The Greek reads "his encampment" (rather than "his outstretched wings") and translates the name Immanuel at the close of the verse as "God is with us."
notes.8:14: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text (and the New Testament quotations in Romans 9:33 and 1 Peter 2:8), the Greek inserts "not," promising that the one who trusts in the Lord will not encounter Him as a stone of stumbling or a rock of falling.
notes.8:20: The Greek reads "the law for help" and "no gifts to give" (reflecting a reading of the Hebrew for "dawn" as "bribe/gift"), differing sharply from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.8:23: This verse corresponds to 9:1 in most English Bibles; the Greek opens with the distinctive imperatives "Drink this first, act swiftly."
notes.9:2: The Septuagint reads "whom You brought down in Your gladness" with a hanging clause resumed by "they shall rejoice," differing from the Masoretic Text ("You have multiplied the nation").
notes.9:5: The Septuagint condenses the Messianic throne names into the single title "Messenger of Great Counsel" (Greek: Megales boules angelos), followed by God's promise of peace upon the rulers and health to Him.
notes.9:6: Here and throughout chapters 9-10, the Greek retains the transliteration Kyrios sabaoth ("Lord of hosts").
notes.9:7: The Septuagint reads "death" (thanaton), reflecting Hebrew consonants read as deber ("pestilence/death") rather than dabar ("word").
notes.9:11: The Septuagint distinctively names "the Greeks" (tous Hellenas) in the west where the Hebrew Masoretic Text names the Philistines.
notes.10:6: The Septuagint reads "command My people" (to emo lao) rather than "charge him against the people of My wrath" as in the Masoretic Text.
notes.10:9: The Septuagint preserves a distinctive geographical list, naming "the region above Babylon and Calneh, where the tower was built" (alluding to Genesis 11) and "Arabia" in place of Carchemish, Arpad, and Hamath.
notes.10:23: Verses 22-23 closely match the Septuagint form quoted by the apostle Paul in Romans 9:27-28, including "a shortened word" (logon syntetmenon).
notes.10:28: Verses 28-31 preserve several Septuagint-distinct place names: Aggai (in both verses 28 and 29, for MT Aiath and Geba), Megiddo (for MT Migron), Sa (for MT Laishah), and Gibbeir (for MT Gebim).
notes.11:2: By translating the final quality in verse 2 as "godliness" (eusebeias) and beginning verse 3 with "the Spirit of the fear of God," the Septuagint enumerates seven distinct endowments of the Spirit.
notes.11:10: The Septuagint reads "He who rises up to rule over the nations; in Him the nations shall hope," wording quoted by Paul in Romans 15:12.
notes.11:11: The Septuagint concludes the list of lands with "from the rising of the sun, and from Arabia," where the Masoretic Text has Hamath and the islands of the sea.
notes.11:14: Greek allophylon ("foreigners") is the Septuagint's standard designation for the Philistines; the Greek reads "in the ships of foreigners" rather than the Masoretic Text's "upon the shoulder of the Philistines."
notes.12:2: The Greek text reads "my God is my Savior" and "my glory and my praise is the Lord," whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads "God is my salvation" and "my strength and song is Yah, the LORD."
notes.12:6: The Greek concludes "in her midst" (referring to Zion in the third person), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads "in your midst."
notes.13:3: Greek gigantes ("giants") renders the Hebrew term for "mighty ones" or "warriors," a characteristic Septuagint rendering also found in Isaiah 14:9.
notes.13:4: "The Lord of hosts" translates Greek Kyrios Sabaoth, where the Septuagint of Isaiah transliterates the Hebrew word for "hosts" or "armies" (also in 13:13; 14:22, 24).
notes.13:12: Greek chrysion to apyron ("unfired gold") refers to pure native gold not refined by fire, and Souphir is the Septuagint's distinct form of Ophir, referring here to a precious stone rather than gold.
notes.13:21: The Septuagint populates Babylon's ruins with sirens (seirenes) and demons (daimonia), followed in verse 22 by onocentaurs (onokentauroi, mythical donkey-centaurs) and hedgehogs (echinoi), rendering obscure Hebrew terms for desert creatures.
notes.14:1: "The sojourner" translates Greek gioras, an Aramaic loanword used in the Septuagint for a resident alien or proselyte joining Israel.
notes.14:12: The Greek uses the third person ("How has the morning star... fallen") rather than direct address, and renders the second clause "he who sent to all the nations" (ho apostellon), where the Masoretic Hebrew has "who laid low the nations."
notes.14:20: The Greek reads "my land" and "my people" (spoken within the lament), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew has "your land" and "your people."
notes.14:29: "Foreigners" (allophyloi, literally "people of another tribe") is the Septuagint's regular term for the Philistines (also in 14:31).
notes.14:31: "There is no way to endure" renders the terse Septuagint idiom ouk estin tou einai (literally "there is not of being," meaning no possibility of remaining or surviving).
notes.15:1: Greek reads "the land of Moab" (Moabeitis) and "the wall of the land of Moab" where the Hebrew text names Ar and Kir of Moab.
notes.15:2: Greek reads "all arms are gashed" (brachiones) rather than the Hebrew "every beard is cut off."
notes.15:7: Greek reads "Arabians" (Arabas), reflecting an alternate vocalization of the Hebrew word for "willows" (likewise in 15:9).
notes.15:9: Greek treats the Hebrew words for "lion" and "the ground" as proper names, "Ariel" and "Admah."
notes.16:6: Greek reads "your divination" (manteia) where the Hebrew text reads "his boastings."
notes.16:7: Greek preserves the distinct place-name "Deseth," corresponding to Kir-hareseth in the Hebrew text.
notes.16:11: Greek reads "like a wall you have renewed," rendering the Hebrew place-name Kir-heres as a phrase describing a rebuilt wall.
notes.16:14: Greek shifts to first-person speech ("And now I say") where the Hebrew text reads "now the Lord has spoken."
notes.17:2: Greek reads "forsaken forever" (eis ton aiona) where the Hebrew text reads "the cities of Aroer."
notes.17:5: Greek "a hard valley" (pharangi sterea) interprets the Hebrew place-name "Valley of Rephaim."
notes.17:9: Greek specifies "the Amorites and the Hivites" fleeing before Israel, where the Hebrew text speaks of forsaken wooded heights and summits.
notes.17:11: Greek renders the difficult Hebrew harvest imagery in terms of receiving and apportioning an inheritance (klerose).
notes.18:2: The Greek reads "hostages" (homera) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "envoys," and uses a future indicative ("swift messengers shall go") rather than an imperative.
notes.18:4: The Greek reads "There shall be security in My city" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "I will be quiet and look from My dwelling place."
notes.18:7: The Greek transliterates the divine title as Kyrios Sabaoth ("Lord of hosts") throughout Isaiah; note also the reversal from "a nation without hope" in 18:2 to "a nation hoping" here.
notes.19:2: The Greek uses the Egyptian administrative term nomos ("district" or "province") rather than the Hebrew "kingdom."
notes.19:10: The Greek specifically names zythos, Egyptian barley beer, reflecting the translators' familiarity with Egyptian life.
notes.19:11: Tanis is the Greek Septuagint name for the Egyptian city of Zoan (also in 19:13).
notes.19:18: The Greek transliterates Hebrew ha-tsedek ("righteousness") as Asedek ("City of Asedek"), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "City of Destruction" (or "City of the Sun").
notes.19:25: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("Blessed be Egypt My people, and Assyria the work of My hands"), the Greek addresses the Jewish diaspora: "My people who is in Egypt, and who is among the Assyrians"; likewise in 19:23 the Greek reads "the Egyptians shall serve the Assyrians."
notes.20:1: The Greek preserves the Septuagint proper names Tanathan (Hebrew Tartan), Azotus (the Hellenistic name for Ashdod), and Arna (Hebrew Sargon).
notes.20:2: The Greek includes "and do so, going naked and barefoot" as part of the Lord's command rather than as a narrative statement of Isaiah's obedience.
notes.20:4: The Greek text here reads kekalymmenous ("covered [with the shame of Egypt]"), whereas some Septuagint manuscripts read anakekalymmenous ("uncovered" or "exposed").
notes.21:2: Greek reads "the envoys of the Persians come against me," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Go up, O Elam; besiege, O Media."
notes.21:3: Greek reads "I did wrong so as not to hear; I made haste not to see," diverging from the Masoretic Text ("I am bowed down so that I cannot hear; I am dismayed so that I cannot see").
notes.21:8: Greek reads "call Uriah to the watchtower" and makes "the Lord" (nominative) the speaker of "I stood continually by day," whereas the Masoretic Text reads "a lion cried out, 'My Lord, I stand continually by day.'"
notes.21:11: Greek reads "Idumea" (Edom) here and "Teman" in verse 14, whereas the Masoretic Text reads "Dumah" and "Tema."
notes.22:1: Greek reads "the Valley of Zion" (also in v. 5) and "vain housetops," whereas the Masoretic Text reads "the Valley of Vision" and simply "housetops."
notes.22:15: Greek transliterates the treasurer's name as Somnas (standard English Shebna), and similarly Chelkias for Hilkiah in verse 20.
notes.22:22: Greek reads "the glory of David" and "he shall rule, and there shall be no one who speaks against him; and he shall shut, and there is no one who opens," differing from the Masoretic Text's "key of the house of David" and fuller opening-and-shutting parallel.
notes.22:23: Greek renders the image personally as "a ruler" here and "the man" in verse 25, rather than the Masoretic Text's "peg."
notes.23:1: Throughout this chapter (vv. 1, 6, 10, 14), the Greek renders Hebrew Tarshish as "Carthage."
notes.23:2: Greek reads "To whom have those who dwell in the island become like, merchants of Phoenicia," where the Masoretic Text has "Be still, inhabitants of the coastland, merchants of Sidon."
notes.23:10: Greek reads "Till your land, for ships no longer come from Carthage," diverging markedly from the Masoretic Text ("Overflow your land like the Nile, O daughter of Tarshish; there is no more restraint").
notes.23:18: Greek concludes with "for a memorial contribution before the Lord," whereas the Masoretic Text reads "for stately clothing."
notes.24:5: Greek enomesen literally reads "acted lawlessly," reflecting the Septuagint rendering in contrast to the Masoretic Hebrew "is defiled."
notes.24:6: The Septuagint reads ptochoi esontai ("shall be poor"), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads "are burned."
notes.24:16: The Septuagint reads "Hope for the godly" and "you who set aside the law," differing distinctly from the Masoretic Text.
notes.24:23: The Septuagint reads the Hebrew homographs for "moon" and "sun" as "the brick" (he plinthos) and "the wall" (to teichos), yielding "the brick shall melt away, and the wall shall fall."
notes.25:2: The Greek text explicitly includes the negative me ("so that their foundations should not fall"), contrasting the fortified cities God upholds with the city of the ungodly that shall never be built.
notes.25:6: Greek Kyrios Sabaoth transliterates the Hebrew title rendered here as "the Lord of hosts."
notes.25:8: Unlike the Masoretic Hebrew ("He will swallow up death forever"), the Septuagint makes "death" (ho thanatos) the grammatical subject: "Death prevailed and swallowed up."
notes.25:11: The masculine pronouns shift from Moab ("he shall let down his hands... just as he himself also brought low") to God ("He shall humble his arrogance"), following the dense Septuagint syntax.
notes.26:13: The Septuagint reads the imperative ktesai hemas ("Possess us"), whereas the Masoretic Text speaks of other lords having ruled over Israel.
notes.26:14: The Septuagint reads the Hebrew consonants for "shades of the dead" as iatroi ("physicians") and "memory" as pan arsen ("every male").
notes.26:17: The Septuagint reads to agapeto sou ("to Your beloved") where the Masoretic Text reads "before You."
notes.26:18: The Septuagint reads positively ("we have accomplished the spirit of Your salvation upon the earth"), whereas the Masoretic Text reads negatively ("we have brought forth wind; we have not accomplished deliverance").
notes.27:1: The Greek describes the sword as "holy, great, and mighty" and omits the Hebrew Masoretic Text's reference to the dragon being in the sea.
notes.27:3: The Septuagint reads "I am a strong city, a besieged city," diverging from the Masoretic Text ("I, the LORD, keep it") through a different reading of the Hebrew consonants.
notes.27:9: The Greek reads "his blessing" where the Masoretic Text has "the full fruit"; the clause "when I take away his sin" is echoed in Romans 11:27.
notes.27:12: "Rhinocorura" (modern El-Arish) is the Septuagint's distinct proper name for the border town marking the Brook of Egypt.
notes.28:1: The Septuagint reads "hirelings of Ephraim" and "drunk without wine," differing from the Masoretic Text's "drunkards of Ephraim" overcome with wine.
notes.28:4: The critical Greek text reads "the hope of life" rather than "glory" at the start of the verse.
notes.28:16: Literally "the Lord, the Lord" (double kyrios). The concluding promise ("he who believes shall by no means be put to shame") is cited in Romans 9:33, 10:11, and 1 Peter 2:6.
notes.28:21: The Greek translates Mount Perazim as "a mountain of the ungodly." The final noun literally means "decay" or "rottenness," often regarded as an early Greek variant for "bitterness."
notes.28:28: The Septuagint uniquely reads that cumin "shall be eaten with bread," followed by God's assurance that He will not be angry forever.
notes.29:3: The Greek reads "like David" where the Masoretic Text has "like a circle," reflecting an ancient interchange between similar Hebrew consonants.
notes.29:5: Following the Greek critical text, this translates "from a wall" rather than the textual variant "from a wheel."
notes.29:22: The Greek reads "whom He set apart from Abraham," whereas the Masoretic Text has "who redeemed Abraham."
notes.29:24: The Septuagint concludes the chapter with the additional promise, "and the stammering tongues shall learn to speak peace."
notes.30:4: The Greek names Tanis (corresponding to Hebrew Zoan) and reads "evil messengers" (angeloi poneroi) where the Masoretic Text refers to the Egyptian city of Hanes.
notes.30:15: The Greek uses the emphatic double title "the Lord, the Lord" (kyrios Kyrios) and reads "when you turn back and groan" (apostrapheis stenaxes), differing from the Masoretic Text's "in returning and rest."
notes.30:20: In verses 20 and 21 the Septuagint reads "those who lead you astray" (hoi planontes se), whereas the Masoretic Text refers to "your Teacher."
notes.30:33: Rather than naming Topheth as in the Masoretic Text, the Greek addresses the ruler directly with a rhetorical question about a deep ravine prepared with fire and wood.
notes.31:3: The Septuagint reads "and there is no help" (kai ouk estin boetheia) where the Masoretic Text has "and not spirit."
notes.31:4: Here and in verse 5, Kyrios sabaoth (transliterating the Hebrew title for armies or hosts) is rendered "the Lord of hosts."
notes.31:9: The Septuagint concludes the chapter with a blessing on those having descendants in Zion and kinsmen in Jerusalem, contrasting with the Masoretic Text's reference to the Lord's fire in Zion and furnace in Jerusalem.
notes.32:5: The Septuagint reads "your servants shall no longer say, 'Be silent!'" (Siga), diverging from the Masoretic Text's saying that the scoundrel will no longer be called generous.
notes.32:15: The Greek treats the Hebrew word for "fruitful field" as a proper name, spelling it Chermel in verse 15 and Karmelo in verse 16 (both rendered "Carmel" here), and makes Carmel the subject that becomes a wilderness in verse 15.
notes.32:19: The Septuagint turns this verse into an assurance that the hail will not fall upon the people and that forest dwellers will dwell securely, whereas the Masoretic Text describes hail bringing down the forest.
notes.33:1: The Greek concludes with the vivid simile 'like a moth upon a garment, so shall they be defeated,' a distinctive Septuagint rendering compared to the Hebrew text.
notes.33:5: The Greek places 'in righteousness' in the dative case at the end of verse 5, linking it syntactically with 'in the law they shall be delivered up' at the opening of verse 6.
notes.33:9: The Greek reads 'Galilee' where the Hebrew text has 'the Arabah,' and transliterates Carmel as 'Chermel.'
notes.33:18: The Greek reads 'those who are nourished' (apparently reflecting an alternate reading of the Hebrew word for 'towers'), and the clause flows directly into the compressed syntax of verse 19.
notes.33:24: The Greek has the inhabitants refrain from saying 'I am weary' (kopio) rather than 'I am sick.'
notes.34:5: Here and in verse 6 the Greek uses the distinct Hellenistic regional name 'Idumea' (Idoumaia) corresponding to Hebrew Edom.
notes.34:11: Here and in verse 14 the Greek renders the desert creatures as 'onocentaurs' (donkey-centaurs), alongside 'sirens' in verse 13, reflecting ancient Greek natural-history and mythological vocabulary.
notes.34:17: The Greek shifts briefly to the second-person plural ('you shall inherit') before returning to the third-person plural ('they shall rest').
notes.35:2: The Greek specifies 'the waste places of the Jordan,' a distinctive Septuagint expansion not found in the Hebrew text.
notes.35:6: 'Stammerers' translates the rare Greek word mogilalos ('speaking with difficulty'), a term notably echoed in Mark 7:32.
notes.35:7: The Greek reads 'gladness of birds' rather than 'haunt of jackals,' and in verse 8 specifies 'the dispersed' walking upon the clean way.
notes.36:7: The Greek text omits the clause found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text concerning Hezekiah's removal of high places and altars, connecting the conditional clause directly into verse 8.
notes.36:9: The Greek text diverges from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, presenting the second clause as a declaration that those who trust in Egypt for horse and rider are household servants.
notes.36:16: The Greek text reads "your bronze vessel" (chalkou), a distinct textual reading where the Hebrew and other Greek witnesses read "your cistern" (lakkou).
notes.36:19: The Greek text uses the distinct place name Eppharuaim where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has Sepharvaim.
notes.37:12: The Greek text names Rapheth and places these cities "in the land of Theemath," differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's Rezeph and "the people of Eden who were in Telassar."
notes.37:13: The Greek text preserves the distinct names Eppharuaim, Anag, and Ugaua where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah.
notes.37:25: The Greek text reads "I have laid a bridge, and I have laid waste the waters and every gathering of water," diverging markedly from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's imagery of digging, drinking, and drying up the streams of Egypt.
notes.37:26: The Greek text reads the first-person verb "Have I not heard" (ekousa) rather than the second-person "Have you not heard" of the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.37:38: The Greek text calls Nisroch Sennacherib's "ancestral deity" (patrarchon) and locates the sons' escape in Armenia, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "his god" and "the land of Ararat."
notes.38:8: The Greek reads "the house of your father" (rather than naming Ahaz) and states explicitly that the sun itself went back up the ten steps down which the shadow had gone.
notes.38:17: The Greek reads "You chose my soul" and uniquely says "behind me" rather than "behind Your back."
notes.38:19: Unlike the Hebrew ("the father makes known to the children"), the Greek has Hezekiah declare that from this day forward he will father children who will proclaim God's righteousness.
notes.38:22: The Greek frames Hezekiah's words as a declarative statement rather than a question.
notes.39:2: "Nechotha" is a Greek transliteration of a Hebrew term for a spice-house or treasure-house; the Greek also speaks of "vessels of the treasure" rather than an armory.
notes.39:5: "Sabaoth" is the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew word for "hosts" or "armies."
notes.39:8: The Greek reads "peace and righteousness" rather than "peace and truth."
notes.40:2: The Greek explicitly addresses "O priests" and speaks of Jerusalem's "humiliation" being fulfilled.
notes.40:5: The Greek reads "the salvation of God" (the wording later cited in Luke 3:6), and in verse 7 omits the clause about the breath of the Lord blowing on the grass.
notes.40:10: The Greek doubles the divine title (kyrios Kyrios), rendered literally here as "the Lord, the Lord."
notes.40:26: The final clause literally reads "nothing has escaped You," shifting to second-person singular (often understood as an apostrophe to God, or alternatively an address to Jacob/Israel).
notes.40:29: The Greek literally states that God gives "sorrow to those who are not in pain," and throughout verses 28-31 uses "hunger" where the Hebrew has "faint."
notes.41:1: Greek reads "Be renewed" (ἐγκαινίζεσθε) before Me, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Keep silence."
notes.41:10: Greek reads "do not go astray" (μὴ πλανῶ), differing from the Hebrew "do not look around in dismay."
notes.41:14: Greek renders "tiny Israel" (ὀλιγοστὸς Ἰσραήλ, literally "few in number"), where the Hebrew text reads "worm Jacob, men of Israel."
notes.41:27: Greek reads "I will give a beginning to Zion, and I will comfort Jerusalem," diverging notably from the Hebrew "First to Zion, 'Behold, here they are!' and to Jerusalem I will give a herald of good news."
notes.42:1: Greek explicitly identifies the servant as "Jacob" and the chosen one as "Israel," names absent from the Hebrew text.
notes.42:4: Greek reads "He shall shine forth" (ἀναλάμψει) and "in his name the nations shall hope" (echoed in Matthew 12:21), where the Hebrew has "he will not grow faint" and "the coastlands wait for his law."
notes.42:6: The Greek critical text ends with "for a covenant of a people" without the phrase "for a light to the nations" found in the Hebrew text and some later Greek manuscripts.
notes.42:10: Greek reads "His dominion" (ἡ ἀρχὴ αὐτοῦ), where the Hebrew text reads "His praise."
notes.42:24: Greek opens with the relative pronoun "to which" (οἷς), linking directly to "the things to come" in verse 23, where the Hebrew text begins a new question, "Who gave Jacob to the looter?"
notes.43:3: "Syene" translates the Septuagint's Soene (an Upper Egyptian border city), where the Masoretic Hebrew reads "Seba."
notes.43:12: The Greek text reads "I reproached" (oneidisa) and the first-person plural "among us" (en hemin), where the Masoretic Hebrew reads "I proclaimed" and "among you."
notes.43:15: The Septuagint reads "who appointed Israel as your king," taking Israel as the object appointed to kingship rather than the Masoretic Hebrew "the Creator of Israel, your King."
notes.43:20: "Sirens and daughters of ostriches" renders the Septuagint's seirenes kai thygateres strouthon, Greek equivalents used for desert creatures corresponding to jackals and ostriches in the Hebrew.
notes.43:26: The Septuagint explicitly supplies "your iniquities" (tas anomias sou) as what Jacob is summoned to declare first in the courtroom dispute.
notes.44:2: "Beloved Israel" translates the Septuagint's ho egapemenos Israel, interpreting the poetic Hebrew name "Jeshurun."
notes.44:6: "God of Sabaoth" preserves the Greek transliteration theos sabaoth (meaning "God of hosts"), and "after these things" follows the Septuagint's meta tauta rather than "the last."
notes.44:21: The Septuagint has the active imperative "do not forget Me" (me epilanthanou mou), whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads passively, "you will not be forgotten by Me."
notes.44:26: "Idumea" preserves the Septuagint reading Idoumaias (Edom), where the Masoretic Hebrew reads "Judah."
notes.44:28: "Who bids Cyrus to be wise" translates the Septuagint's ho legon Kyro phronein, where the Masoretic Hebrew reads "who says of Cyrus, 'He is My shepherd.'"
notes.45:1: The Greek text reads "that nations may obey before him," "the strength of kings," and "cities," diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("to subdue nations," "loins of kings," and "gates").
notes.45:4: The Greek reads "by My name" and "I will accept you," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "by your name" and "I have surnamed you."
notes.45:9: The Greek opens with two distinctive rhetorical questions concerning potter's clay and a plowman, where the Hebrew text pronounces a woe upon one who strives with his Maker.
notes.45:13: The Greek adds "as king" and transliterates the divine title as Kyrios Sabaoth ("the Lord of hosts"), as also in 45:14 and 47:4.
notes.45:15: The Greek reads "and we did not know it" and omits "Savior," contrasting with the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "a God who hides Himself... the Savior."
notes.46:1: Together with verse 2, the Greek portrays the idols as bound up like a burden for a weary, hungry bearer who cannot be saved from war, differing markedly from the Hebrew text.
notes.46:4: The Greek future verb meaning "I will forgive" or "I will remit" reflects a different sense of the underlying Hebrew verb than the Masoretic sense "I will bear."
notes.46:11: The Greek reads "concerning the things I have purposed" rather than "the man of My counsel," and includes the additional closing clause "I led him and made his way prosperous."
